articles.headline: Eisenkot chosen over Netanyahu to form Israel’s next government
articles.title: Eisenkot chosen over Netanyahu to form Israel’s next government
articles.description: Israel's president asked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next gov't over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.headline: Israeli president tasks opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
articles.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog has selected opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to attempt forming a new coalition administration following inconclusive election results in Israel. Eisenkot received sixty-seven recommendations in the Knesset parliament compared to forty-six for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The candidate has twenty-eight days to build a stable government, which aims to resolve political deadlock after neither major bloc secured an outright majority.
articles.description: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.

articles.headline: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming new government
articles.title: Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has selected former army chief Gadi Eisenkot to form the country's next government, passing over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, received recommendations from 67 lawmakers compared to 46 for Netanyahu. Eisenkot faces a 28-day deadline to build a coalition holding at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
articles.description: Isaac Herzog formally gives Gadi Eisenkot 28 days to secure 61 Knesset seats and replace Netanyahu as prime minister.

articles.headline: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming new government
articles.title: Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government following an inconclusive election. Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief, must navigate complex coalition negotiations within a 28-day window after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in the October 27 vote while remaining the largest bloc in parliament.
articles.description: Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament

articles.headline: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and placed under house arrest
articles.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Asuncion voted unanimously on November 7, 2026, to impeach and arrest Paraguayan President Santiago Pena following the collapse of Ueno Bank. The financial crisis left millions of citizens without access to savings, prompting massive protests and corruption charges against Pena, who denied wrongdoing before Vice-President Pedro Alliana assumed the interim presidency.
articles.description: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.

articles.headline: US bombs Qeshm island as regional mediators attempt to prevent wider conflict
articles.title: Qeshm island and Hormuz hit, as mediators try to prevent US-Iran escalation
articles.summary: United States military forces carried out air strikes hitting Qeshm island in Iran on Friday night, according to officials, amid escalating maritime tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes follow numerous attacks on commercial vessels in the region over recent weeks. Meanwhile, Iranian officials stated that military limitations on ballistic missile ranges have been lifted in response to ongoing foreign threats.
articles.description: US strikes have continued on Iran after more ships in the Strait of Hormuz were attacked.

articles.headline: Trump confirms US strikes in Iran, insists ‘it’s not a war’
articles.title: Trump confirms US strikes in Iran, insists ‘it’s not a war’
articles.description: US President Donald Trump said America has carried out ‘minor strikes’ on Iran’s Qeshm Island.

articles.headline: U.S. military executes targeted airstrikes on Iran amid ongoing nuclear negotiations
articles.title: U.S. military carries out fresh targeted strikes on Iran as Tehran weighs mediator's proposals
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump confirmed that American forces conducted limited military strikes on an Iranian air defence system on November 6, 2026. The operation occurred as Qatari mediators advanced proposals for a bridge deal to address differences over Tehran's nuclear programme, though Iranian officials insisted on several core concessions before engaging in formal talks.
articles.description: ‘They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,’ says U.S. President Trump

articles.headline: Trump confirms targeted American military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
articles.title: Trump confirms new US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that American forces carried out minor strikes against Iranian air defence installations on Qeshm Island. Iranian state media reported explosions and the downing of a United States drone, while Qatari officials dismissed rumours that negotiations between Washington and Tehran had failed following recent midterm elections.
articles.description: The US president also claims 'a lot of progress' in Washington's negotiations with Tehran.

articles.headline: OpenAI secures funding valuation of $1.25 trillion
articles.title: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
articles.summary: According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has reached a valuation of $1.25 trillion after securing another $11 billion in funding. Meanwhile, rival company Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week. OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman stated that the organization is currently prioritizing safety measures over pursuing an initial public offering in the near future.
articles.description: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. That would make it one of the world's most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion. Echoing FT and Wall Street Journal […]

articles.headline: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to Chief of Staff ‘to run things well’
articles.title: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to Chief of Staff ‘to run things well’
articles.description: President Donald Trump has promoted long-time aide Stephen Miller to Chief of Staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

articles.headline: Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff
articles.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on November 6, 2026, that Stephen Miller is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff following the Republican midterm defeats. Wiles, the first woman in the post, is moving to the Trump Political Operation. Miller has been a close adviser and speechwriter since 2016.
articles.description: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

articles.headline: Donald Trump appoints Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
articles.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles resigned following Republican midterm losses. Democratic lawmakers criticized the appointment of Miller, who has been a key architect of administration immigration policies, amid expectations of congressional investigations starting in January.
articles.description: Susie Wiles steps down as White House chief of staff; Stephen Miller assumes the role amid post-election reshuffling.

articles.headline: Global tech stocks tumble following U.S. midterm election results
articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.summary: Global technology stocks slumped after United States midterm election results raised concerns over tighter regulatory scrutiny for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, 2026, erasing $2.53 trillion in market value. Semiconductor firms bore significant losses, though Indian equities bucked the trend with a strong rally as foreign investors bought shares.
articles.description: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

articles.headline: Former Paraguay President Santiago Peña charged over bank collapse
articles.title: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
articles.summary: Prosecutors in Asuncion charged deposed leader Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain following the collapse of Ueno Bank. Judge Humberto Otazu ordered Mr Peña to be held at a military base during investigations. The bank failure froze millions of accounts, triggering Congress to remove Mr Peña and replace him with Pedro Alliana, while public protests and an upcoming teachers union strike persist.
articles.description: In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm

articles.headline: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.title: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk describes a deadly shooting in Krakow that killed six people as an act of ‘terrorism’.

articles.headline: Explosions reported in southern Iran as two oil tankers catch fire
articles.title: Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report
articles.summary: Explosions were reported on November 7, 2026, in southern Iran including Qeshm Island, according to Iranian state television, while the Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Officials did not confirm missile strikes, though U.S. forces recently struck the island, raising regional tensions amid ongoing shipping conflicts.
articles.description: State TV said Iranian ‌officials have not confirmed any missile strikes on the areas, while the semi-official Tasnim news agency cited ‌a source as saying that the explosions heard ‌on ⁠Qeshm Island were not related to missile strikes

articles.headline: U.S. military disables cargo vessel attempting to break blockade
articles.title: U.S. military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman
articles.summary: An American military aircraft fired precision munitions and disabled a St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel on November 7, 2026, after it tried to leave regional waters following an Iranian port visit, the U.S. Central Command stated. The command also launched a task force to target advanced weapon smuggling, estimating its naval blockade has blocked over $25 billion in crude oil exports.
articles.description: The St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel tried to ‌depart regional waters after visiting ‌an ⁠Iranian port, and a U.S. plane fired precision munitions at its stern after U.S. forces ​directed the crew to ‌abandon targeted spaces, Central Command said

articles.headline: Six killed and fifteen injured in Krakow mass shooting
articles.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
articles.summary: At least six people died and fifteen others sustained injuries after a gunman opened fire on random individuals in central Krakow's Main Market Square. Armed officers engaged the suspect, who was subsequently arrested at the scene. Polish authorities confirmed the attacker wore military-style attire, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk traveled to the city as investigations into the background and circumstances continue.
articles.description: Six people were killed in a random shooting in the city's main square, and three bodies were later found at his home.

articles.headline: Police clash with protesters as anti-government rallies sweep France
articles.title: Police clash with protesters as anti-government rallies sweep France
articles.description: Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as Yellow Vests defied a ban on their rally, leading to arrests.

articles.headline: Defence minister Rajnath Singh calls for highest military preparedness at Bagdogra Air Force station
articles.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
articles.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged armed forces personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station in West Bengal to maintain high operational readiness amid an increasingly complex security landscape. Speaking near the frontier with China, Singh highlighted emerging threats including cyber attacks, proxy wars, and misinformation campaigns, while reaffirming the government's push for indigenous defence technologies through start-ups.
articles.description: Addressing personnel at key airbase near China frontier, Defence Minister warns of adversaries exploiting ‘vulnerabilities’; he also reviews Army’s LAC infrastructure, operational preparedness and lauds initiatives aimed at strengthening ties with local communities

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India data shows cash usage remains unchanged
articles.title: 10 years since demonetisation: Cash usage unchanged, fake notes on the rise
articles.summary: Ten years after demonetisation, Reserve Bank of India data indicates that the policy had minimal impact on reducing overall cash in circulation while counterfeit note detections rose, particularly for 500 rupee notes. Meanwhile, Unified Payments Interface transaction values have experienced steady year-over-year growth relative to India Gross Domestic Product according to the official figures.
articles.description: This Deepavali marks 10 years since Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced overnight demonetisation of 86% of the country’s cash. Data shows some stated aims of the move remain largely unmet

articles.headline: Thousands of demonstrators protest across France against rising cost of living
articles.title: More than 140,000 rally as new protests against rising costs sweep France
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of protesters rallied across France for a fourth consecutive weekend to demonstrate against the rising cost of living. The Ministry of the Interior reported 146,000 participants nationwide, while unions estimated 250,000 demonstrators. The protests involved heavy security deployments, clashes in Paris and Lyon, and occurred ahead of the presidential election scheduled for April.
articles.description: Tear gas fired in Paris and Lyon as interior minister warns authorities are 'ready and waiting' for rioters and looters.

articles.headline: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia faces threat as Russian drones close in
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia faces threat as Russian drones close in
articles.description: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, once a refuge for those fleeing the war, is now facing growing danger.

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials to discuss ceasefire
articles.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
articles.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations to the White House to discuss a six-day ceasefire in the Kherson region. The truce allowed for the evacuation of residents from Oleshky. While officials praised the humanitarian progress, some analysts suggest the move was orchestrated by Vladimir Putin to influence US midterm elections.
articles.description: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump orders Department of Justice to investigate Democrats
articles.title: Trump orders DOJ to investigate Democrats for ‘threatening’ people
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump directed the Department of Justice to investigate Democratic lawmakers for alleged threats following their midterm election victory. Writing on social media, Trump claimed without evidence that Democratic probes into his administration and associates amounted to criminal extortion. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November elections, granting them investigative powers.
articles.description: Trump lashed out at Democrats on Truth Social days after the party won control of Congress.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces report battlefield advances as deadly strikes hit Sanaa
articles.title: Yemeni gov’t forces report advances as Houthis say deadly strikes hit Sanaa
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces reported repelling Houthi assaults and advancing in Marib and al-Jawf provinces during ongoing military operations. Meanwhile, the Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that air strikes killed at least 27 people and wounded about 30 others in al-Shariya village in Sanaa province. The Houthis blamed the Saudi-led coalition, while Al Jazeera could not independently verify the competing claims.
articles.description: Civilians bear the brunt of fighting as 27 people reported killed in strikes on a village in Sanaa province.

articles.headline: Democratic party sweeps United States midterm elections
articles.title: Why are the U.S. midterm elections significant?
articles.summary: United States voters ended President Donald Trump's federal government trifecta control during the midterm elections held on November 8, 2026. Democrats triumphed by capturing historically red states and maintaining key strongholds alongside essential swing states. Consequently, the Republican Party surrendered control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, altering the national political balance significantly.
articles.description: What do the results tell us about American voters’ attitudes towards President Donald Trump? What do they mean for Democrats and Republicans? What lies ahead for Democrats? Why are these results so important for the rest of the world?

articles.headline: US offers twenty million dollars for Iran nuclear details
articles.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced a reward of up to twenty million dollars for information regarding Iran's nuclear programme, including facilities, equipment, and associated personnel. Meanwhile, United States Central Command established Task Force Iron Gate to restrict weapons movement and sanctioned material across Iranian borders, while regional mediators continued efforts to negotiate an end to the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.

articles.headline: Houthis report 25 killed in Yemen strikes
articles.title: Houthis report 25 killed in Yemen strikes
articles.description: Yemen’s Houthis say at least 25 people have been killed and 30 injured in air strikes.

articles.headline: Twenty five killed in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen
articles.title: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
articles.summary: Media outlets linked to the Houthi movement reported that at least twenty five individuals, including women and children, died following Saudi airstrikes in al-Shariyah. The attack occurred amid resumed major fighting across Yemen between the Houthis and forces supporting the internationally recognised government. The United Nations stated that more than one thousand six hundred people have died since hostilities reignited.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

articles.headline: Ukraine says Russia intensifies strikes ahead of diplomatic peace talks
articles.title: Ukraine says Russia ramps up strikes to pressure Kyiv at talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles on November 7, 2026, causing widespread power outages across five regions. The Energy Ministry reported severe transmission disruptions in Kyiv. Mr. Zelenskyy alleged Moscow aims to exert pressure ahead of U.S.-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, while the Russian Defence Ministry confirmed strikes on military and energy infrastructure.
articles.description: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region

articles.headline: Yemeni Houthis launch drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi sites
articles.title: Saudi oil sites, troops and Riyadh airport targeted: Houthis
articles.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement carried out six military operations on November 7, 2026, targeting Saudi troops and infrastructure. According to military spokesperson Yahya Saree, the strikes hit Aramco oil facilities, Riyadh airport, and military installations on both sides of the border amid an ongoing conflict involving a Saudi-led coalition.
articles.description: The Iran-backed group, which is fighting a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government, allegedly launched six operations

articles.headline: Gunman kills five people during shooting attack in Krakow
articles.title: Gunman kills 5, injures 12 in Poland’s Krakow shooting attack
articles.summary: Five individuals died and over a dozen suffered injuries after an armed perpetrator opened fire randomly from a vehicle in Krakow's Main Square on November 7, 2026. Local police confirmed that law enforcement officers were among the wounded and that the suspect sustained injuries during a police confrontation. Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that an official investigation is currently underway in Poland's second-largest city.
articles.description: The gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's Main Square, Krakow police said

articles.headline: Israel builds 90km network of military roads across southern Lebanon
articles.title: Israel builds 90km network of military roads across southern Lebanon
articles.description: Israel is building roads and military outposts across southern Lebanon.

articles.headline: World Bank brief highlights extreme poverty decline and high prosperity gap
articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.summary: According to a World Bank brief, India experienced a significant decline in extreme poverty between 2011 and 2023, with hundreds of millions moving out of poverty. However, the report highlights a high prosperity gap driven by flat real earnings, low-productivity work, and rising youth unemployment, indicating that many individuals require substantial income increases to reach prosperity.
articles.description: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

articles.headline: Five killed and at least 10 injured in Krakow shooting
articles.title: Five killed and at least 10 injured in Krakow shooting
articles.description: Five people have been killed and at least 10 injured in a shooting near the main market square in Krakow, Poland.

articles.headline: New Zealand general election ends without clear winner as major parties prepare for talks
articles.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
articles.summary: New Zealand faced political uncertainty following a tight general election where Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party won forty-two seats and the Labour Party secured thirty-six. With neither major party achieving a majority, smaller groups like the Opportunity Party emerged as potential kingmakers. According to polling experts, cost of living pressures heavily influenced voter sentiment during the contest.
articles.description: Weeks of coalition talks could follow after preliminary results pointed to a highly divided national parliament.

articles.headline: Allahabad High Court criticises Uttar Pradesh Police over routine violations of fundamental rights
articles.title: Allahabad High Court slams U.P. Police over routine violations of fundamental rights
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court strongly criticised the Uttar Pradesh Police for routine infringements on civil liberties while ordering the release of a petitioner who was allegedly detained unlawfully. Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev rejected the state's excuse regarding a malfunctioning CCTV system caused by a thunderstorm, noting that footage appeared to be deliberately withheld. The court also ordered the state to pay twenty thousand rupees in litigation costs.
articles.description: Ordering the release of a petitioner whose family alleged that he was forcibly picked up by police in plain clothes on September 5, the Bench says police appear to have little regard for constitutional freedoms

articles.headline: Five people killed in shooting near Krakow market square in Poland
articles.title: At least six people killed in shooting in Poland’s Krakow
articles.summary: Five people were killed and about a dozen others wounded during a shooting incident near the main market square in Krakow, Poland. Police stated that a gunman fired at random people from a vehicle before being neutralised by officers and transported to hospital. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed the attack on social media, confirming that authorities were actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the tragic event.
articles.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says police are investigating after 'tragic shooting' in second-largest city.

articles.headline: Airstrikes in al-Shariya village near Sanaa kill twenty-two people
articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
articles.summary: Attacks hit several homes in al-Shariya village near the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on November 7, 2026, resulting in twenty-two deaths and thirty injuries, mostly among women and children, according to Anees Alasbahi, a spokesman for the Houthi-run Health Ministry. Alasbahi attributed the assault to Saudi Arabia, though the claim remained unverified and the Saudi Information Ministry did not immediately respond. The incident follows a November 6 market strike in southern Yemen that killed at least thirty people amid escalating conflict between the Iranian-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed forces.
articles.description: Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

articles.headline: Russian drone and missile attacks escalate across Zaporizhzhia region
articles.title: ‘They started bombing us with drones’: Russian attacks unnerve Zaporizhzhia
articles.summary: Escalating Russian drone and missile strikes have forced residents from villages like Preobrazhenka into shelters in the Ukrainian regional capital of Zaporizhzhia. The attacks include a November 2 strike in Komyshuvakha that killed at least fifty people, alongside recent hits on bridges, shopping malls, and buses. Regional military administration official Denys Knysh stated that authorities are prepared to evacuate the city if security conditions deteriorate further, while displaced residents and local workers express fear and uncertainty regarding the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: A region once offering refuge becomes increasingly dangerous, as 50 people are killed in a single attack.

articles.headline: Gaza displacement camps collapse under rainwater
articles.title: Gaza displacement camps collapse under rainwater
articles.description: Rainwater is inundating displacement camps across Gaza as makeshift shelters collapse. Al Jazeera’s Nour Khaled reports.

articles.headline: Heavy rain floods Gaza camps and damages unsafe buildings
articles.title: Buildings damaged in Israeli bombings risk collapse as rain inundates Gaza
articles.summary: Severe storms and heavy rain on November 7, 2026, flooded displacement camps and damaged structures across the Gaza Strip, leaving thousands of displaced Palestinians shivering in soaked shelters. Water levels rose by thirty to forty centimetres in multiple camps, including al-Mina, while damaged buildings in Nuseirat faced collapse risks. Officials from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and the Gaza Municipality reported severe shortages of shelter supplies, fuel, and equipment to handle the widespread flooding and structural dangers.
articles.description: Floods have swept through Gaza after heavy rain, endangering families and putting war-damaged buildings at risk.

articles.headline: Heavy rains flood displacement camps across Gaza
articles.title: Heavy rains flood displacement camps across Gaza
articles.description: Heavy rains and strong winds have flooded and damaged displacement tents across Gaza.

articles.headline: Russian drone and missile strikes cause widespread blackouts across Ukraine
articles.title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that overnight Russian missile and drone attacks damaged energy infrastructure across 12 Ukrainian regions, leaving the capital Kyiv facing severe power, water, and heating disruptions. The bombardment involved over 30 ballistic missiles and 170 drones, injuring nine people. These strikes occurred ahead of upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi and followed a recent humanitarian evacuation in Oleshky.
articles.description: The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

articles.headline: New report reveals artificial intelligence is accelerating Anthropic research development
articles.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
articles.summary: A report published Thursday by the artificial intelligence safety research organization METR revealed that Anthropic models are improving twice as fast as last year largely due to artificial intelligence assistance. The findings highlight significant productivity gains among employees using unreleased internal models. However, researchers noted that Anthropic heavily redacted the public report to protect sensitive competitive information from rivals.
articles.description: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down. That's according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation […]

articles.headline: Tankers carrying Russian diesel change course amid ongoing US trader hesitation
articles.title: Why are oil traders refusing to buy Russian diesel after Trump-Putin deal?
articles.summary: At least three tankers carrying Russian diesel have altered their destinations away from the United States following a temporary sanctions exemption agreed between President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in October. Traders remain hesitant to purchase the fuel due to continued congressional bans and legal risks. While Moscow insists the trade will proceed, experts state the initial shipments will provide minimal relief to high American fuel prices.
articles.description: Zero Russian diesel has reached the US as tankers divert and buyers fear legal action.

articles.headline: Dozens killed in Yemen market strike as government offensive against Houthis continues
articles.title: Dozens killed as humanitarian crisis mounts in Yemen: What next for war?
articles.summary: A missile strike killed dozens of people at a market in the Taiz governorate on Friday, with Yemen's internationally recognized government and the Houthi movement blaming each other for the attack. The violence coincides with an ongoing month-long military offensive launched by the Presidential Leadership Council to reclaim territory. The protracted conflict has displaced hundreds of thousands of people and deepened a severe humanitarian crisis across the nation.
articles.description: Government forces reclaim key territories in Taiz and Lahij but face setbacks under Houthi resistance in certain areas.

articles.headline: Winter storm floods tens of thousands of displaced families' tents in Gaza
articles.title: Rains flood 70,000 displaced families’ tents in Gaza
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall from the first winter storm of the season flooded approximately 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Gaza Strip within 12 hours. According to Gaza's Government Media Office, the disaster caused initial losses estimated at three million dollars, collapsed walls, and triggered about 1,500 distress calls. Officials blamed Israeli restrictions on shelter materials for blocking reconstruction efforts.
articles.description: Initial losses are estimated at about $3m, according to Gaza's Government Media Office.

articles.headline: New Zealand election remains too close to call
articles.title: New Zealand vote still too close to call as results trickle in
articles.summary: New Zealand's general election on November 7, 2026, remained tightly contested as early vote counts showed Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and the opposition Labour Party neck-and-neck. With neither party projected to win an outright majority, attention turned to minor factions like the centrist Opportunity Party. Voters faced rising living costs and economic pressures driven by global fuel shocks.
articles.description: New Zealand’s election remained too close to call on November 7, as early results trickled in from across the country, with neither the governing National-Luxon coalition nor Labour falling short of a majority and minor parties weighing in, including a rising Opportunity Party

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi discusses new memoir and political history in interview
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi interview: ‘Great damage done to the fabric of India by BJP’
articles.summary: In an interview with The Hindu regarding her forthcoming book Belonging: A Journey of Love published by HarperCollins India, senior Indian National Congress politician Sonia Gandhi answered questions from N. Ram about her life, the Emergency, and Indian politics. Gandhi reflected on her decades in India, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi and Indira Gandhi, and her decision to author her own story.
articles.description: Ahead of the launch of her book, Sonia Gandhi speaks to The Hindu, answering a number of questions — personal and political

articles.headline: Sudan child malnutrition crisis deepens amid civil war and drought
articles.title: Sudan war and climate change see parents struggle to feed their children
articles.summary: Severe acute malnutrition is threatening hundreds of thousands of young children across Sudan due to ongoing civil war, displacement, and drought. Medical personnel at facilities like Port Sudan Teaching Hospital report extreme overcrowding and financial strains. According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, hundreds of thousands of children under five are expected to suffer from severe acute malnutrition in 2026, while conflict zones like Darfur and Blue Nile State face worsening humanitarian conditions and inadequate aid.
articles.description: War, poverty and climate change are all affecting Sudanese, with increasing cases of child malnutrition.

articles.headline: State security forces restrict access to proposed Siang dam site
articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.summary: Central security forces and State police have deployed barricades and concertina wires near Parong village in Arunachal Pradesh to restrict unauthorized access to the Siang river. Parong in Siang district is one of three proposed locations identified for a Pre-Feasibility Report regarding the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.
articles.description: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

articles.headline: Trump appoints Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff
articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff on November 6, 2026. Miller, 41, replaces Susie Wiles following a Republican defeat in the midterms. Known for his hardline immigration policies and mass deportation plans, Miller's appointment drew praise from the Make America Great Again movement but severe condemnation from Democratic leaders including Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.
articles.description: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigns amid violent banking protests
articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of protesters flooded the streets of Asuncion on November 4, 2026, after being locked out of their accounts at the countrys largest bank, prompting President Santiago Pena to resign. As Congress moved to impeach him, Senator Antonio Velazquez stated on November 5 that Pena had disappeared and likely fled to Argentina to seek asylum following the unrest.
articles.description: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

articles.headline: Democrats win key gubernatorial races across the United States
articles.title: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured major gubernatorial victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia, and Wisconsin during the elections held on November 4, 2026. Several contenders achieved historic milestones, including Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming Georgia's first Black female governor and Gina Hinojosa becoming Texas's first Latina governor. Voters focused heavily on the cost of living and President Donald Trump's unpopularity, according to U.S. media projections.
articles.description: Hinojosa becomes Texas’s first Latina governor, Bottoms the first Black woman elected governor in the US, and Haaland the first Native American woman to lead a state

articles.headline: Kenyan court sentences doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
articles.summary: Justice Diana Mochache handed down a 200-year prison sentence to Paul Mackenzie on November 6, 2026, following the deaths of 191 individuals in Shakahola forest. The leader of Good News International Ministries was found guilty of homicide and starvation-related offences after instructing followers to fast. Prosecutors had requested the death penalty, but the judge declined the punishment.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

articles.headline: Trump signals willingness to work with Democrats following midterm losses
articles.title: Veto or deals: Can Trump find a way to work with Democrats?
articles.summary: Following midterm elections where Democrats secured majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate, United States President Donald Trump stated he would be willing to work with the opposition. According to University College London lecturer Andrew Proctor, the president faces legislative gridlock because Democrats lack a two-thirds majority to override vetoes. articles.description: Trump has three options to affect legislation, say analysts: veto legislation, enforce executive orders or make deals.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi drone over Medina region
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it downs Houthi drone over Medina; Houthis deny attack

articles.headline: Zaporizhia aid strike death toll reaches fifty three amid ongoing rescue efforts

articles.headline: Intercity school bus crash in eastern France leaves two dead

articles.description: News broadcaster BFM TV reported that the passengers included children travelling to middle and high schools in the area, with a photo from the scene showing the bus had veered off the road and landed in a ditch

articles.headline: Magnitude 5.7 earthquake strikes central Japan and injures dozens
articles.title: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
articles.summary: A strong tremor originating in Shizuoka Prefecture affected a wide area of central Japan, damaging store windows and halting normal transport speeds. According to local media, at least 22 people sustained injuries while evacuating buildings. The Japan Meteorological Agency recorded the magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey measured it at 5.5, with Shizuoka and Aichi experiencing the most severe shaking.
articles.description: A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu

articles.headline: Iran intensifies diplomatic outreach amid renewed United States military threats

Concurrently, Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei traveled to Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss bilateral ties and economic cooperation.
articles.description: Iran launches diplomatic offensive as US mulls resumption of war.

articles.headline: Kenyan court sentences starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie to prison

Twenty-eight accomplices received various prison terms for their roles in the doomsday sect tragedies investigated by authorities since 2023.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie and accomplices were convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets rally as Sensex jumps 1,718 points
articles.title: Stock markets on fire; Sensex jumps 1,718 points, Nifty reclaims 25,000

articles.summary: Moscow agreed to provide Tehran with ninety advanced missile launchers designed for attack helicopters under a 2024 accord, according to reports published on November 6, 2026. articles.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona
articles.summary: Real Madrid secured a three to zero victory against ten-man Valencia at Mestalla Stadium to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona. articles.description: Valverde and Guler's first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.

articles.title: We lost the elections to the Supreme Court, not to the BJP: Mamata-Trinamool’s Abhishek Banerjee
articles.summary: Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee alleged on November 6, 2026, that his party lost the West Bengal Assembly elections to the Supreme Court rather than the Bharatiya Janata Party. articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India resolved a long-running dispute on November 6, 2026, directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to Himachal Pradesh over 20 years. articles.description: SC said Punjab and Haryana will pay Himachal Pradesh 11,973 million units of electricity over a period of 20 years.

articles.description: As of 9 p.m., the TDP wins 229 ZPTCs and 4,823 MPTCs, JSP 36 and 644, BJP eight and 130, and YSRCP 20 and 1,050; TDP upsets YSRCP by wresting Pulivendula ZPTC; fruit of good governance, says Lokesh

articles.headline: European security fears rise amid hybrid attacks
articles.title: Who is behind Europe’s suspected hybrid attacks?
articles.summary: Civilian infrastructure across Europe faces an ongoing wave of security threats involving false bomb hoaxes that disrupted aviation and cyberattacks targeting supermarket freezers. Italy stated that continental infrastructure is currently under attack. Security experts discussed potential coordination behind these incidents, while nations grapple with how to counter the aggression effectively and protect public services from further disruption.
articles.description: Bomb hoaxes and supermarket cyberattacks are heightening security fears.

articles.headline: Writer Jeyamohan depicts historical temple elephant transfer in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Jumbo hustle: the transfer of elephants to Tamil Nadu’s temples
articles.summary: The book Mathagam by writer Jeyamohan features Kesavan, an elephant at the Adi Kesava Perumal Temple in Thiruvattar, to illustrate the shifting status of temple animals in Tamil Nadu. The story contrasts Kesavan's former royal favour and feared authority with his subsequent subjugation as a common working animal following the king death.
articles.description: The unseemly haste with which five elephants from Assam were transported to temples in Tamil Nadu raises pertinent questions about the process of animal transfer, and whether the rules are cheat proof. Here, Geetha Srimathi examines the entire issue threadbare, explaining how elephants are acquired for temples in the State, and the yawning gaps in the rules, and processes that allow humans to ‘trade’ in pachyderms.

articles.headline: Global markets plunge as US tech stock rout spreads to Asia
articles.title: Tech stock rout, driven by US AI fears, continues in Asian trading
articles.summary: Asian trading faced severe disruptions on November 6, 2026, as a United States tech stock rout triggered market suspensions and sharp losses. Analysts attribute the downturn to fears that recent Democratic midterm victories will increase regulatory scrutiny on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Major indices including Japan's Nikkei dropped significantly while regional authorities intervened to stabilize local financial markets.
articles.description: Global markets are being roiled due to concerns over US data centre expansion and AI regulation.

articles.headline: Trump proposes UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary role
articles.title: Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on November 7, 2026, that he asked Ultimate Fighting Championship chief executive Dana White to become White House press secretary. Writing on Truth Social, Trump also requested six current or former titleholders to serve as assistants. Neither White nor TKO Group Holdings immediately responded to requests for comment regarding the proposal.
articles.description: Mr. White, ⁠chief executive of ⁠the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Mr. Trump wrote in ​a Truth ‌Social post

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticises Modi government over voter ID welfare scheme linkage proposal
articles.title: Not just vote theft, it's rights theft: Rahul Gandhi on Centre's 'Voter ID for welfare schemes' remark
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi condemned government proposals on November 6, 2026, to replace Aadhaar with voter IDs for identifying welfare beneficiaries, calling the move a rights violation. Responding to remarks by Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Gandhi alleged that voter roll revisions are being used to manipulate electoral outcomes and restrict access to essential public schemes.
articles.description: Rahul Gandhi termed as a "conspiracy" the Modi Government Minister's announcement that benefits of schemes will now be determined not by Aadhaar, but by Voter ID

articles.headline: Somalia supreme court rejects president term extension amid growing political crisis
articles.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
articles.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his mandate, worsening a constitutional standoff following the disputed dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed. The court ordered leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, challenging government timelines amid ongoing security threats from al-Shabaab militants across the country.
articles.description: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

articles.headline: Jharkhand High Court sets aside cancellation of JSSC-CGL exam
articles.title: Jharkhand HC quashes State Govt decision to cancel JSSC-CGL exam
articles.summary: On November 6, 2026, the Jharkhand High Court quashed the State government's decision to cancel the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level exam and ordered the reinstatement of selected candidates with continuous service. The court stated the government failed to prove systemic irregularities, ruling that individual suspects should be investigated instead of terminating all appointments from the August 17, 2026 cancellation.
articles.description: The court has ordered the reinstatement of the candidates selected under advertisement number 10/2023, directing that their service be treated as continuous, without any interruption.

articles.headline: Devendra Nath Mahto launches yatra after Ranchi student protests
articles.title: Taking reforms to the road: From Ranchi protest to a Statewide yatra
articles.summary: On August 24, 2026, student leader Devendra Nath Mahto launched the Bharti Vyavastha Sudhar Yatra from Nemra village in Ramgarh district. Just six days after ending a 16-day hunger strike and student protests in Ranchi, the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader began the second phase of his campaign demanding examination system reforms and government accountability.
articles.description: The students’ protest in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand’s recruitment exams for government jobs has remained in the news for most of August. Amit Bhelari examines the fallout of the government’s decision to cancel exams, which has left both aspiring candidates and already-appointed government employees caught in the dispute. It has pushed student leader Devendra Nath Mahto from a prolonged protest in Ranchi to a Statewide yatra demanding transparency, accountability and reforms in the government recruitment system

articles.headline: Former Indian women's hockey coach Gurdial Singh Bhangu passes away
articles.title: India hockey coach Gurdial Singh Bhangu dies at 86
articles.summary: Gurdial Singh Bhangu, who coached India to a historic gold medal at the 2002 Commonwealth Games, has died in Surrey, Canada, at the age of 86. Hockey India confirmed the death of the Dronacharya Award winner, whose tactical instructions during the dramatic final against England secured the tournament victory. Bhangu previously coached the Nigerian women's team.
articles.description: Bhangu’s name will forever be associated with one of the most memorable victories in Indian women’s hockey: India’s 3-2 victory over England in the final at Manchester, becoming Commonwealth Games champions

articles.description: Isaac Herzog held a second day of consultations with political parties on November 5 after the October 27 election; he said he will announce on November 8 whom he will task with trying to form a new government

articles.headline: Towhid Hridoy hits record-breaking double century for Bangladesh against West Indies
articles.title: Towhid Hridoy hits record-breaking double century for Bangladesh in second Test against West Indies

articles.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case

articles.headline: Cancer patients in Karnataka face high treatment costs

A senior Iranian lawmaker stated that Tehran receives medicine and political backing in return, while collecting transit fees from India and China. Analysts suggest the move generates revenue and challenges Washington's naval blockade amid the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Tehran says ships from four countries can cross Hormuz freely, but analysts say the deals carry political risks.

articles.headline: Mathematics forms foundational basis for artificial intelligence advancement
articles.title: Mathematics key to AI’s advancement, says expert
articles.summary: Advanced artificial intelligence capabilities and logical reasoning rely fundamentally on mathematical equations, frameworks, and data algorithms according to Reheena Nasrin from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology. Speaking at an international conference organised by Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education, experts emphasised that mathematical foundations remain critical for future digital intelligence development alongside presentations of more than two hundred research papers.

articles.headline: Pope Leo holds first mass in Uruguay and urges crowd to be bridge builders
articles.title: Pope Leo hold first mass in Uruguay, urges crowd to be ‘bridge builders’
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV addressed more than 30,000 attendees at Paris London Park in Paysandu during his first mass in western Uruguay on Saturday. The Roman Catholic Church head urged the crowd to share their faith and act as bridge builders. The pontiff is on a 12-day tour of Latin America that includes Argentina and Peru.
articles.description: Vatican says some 40,000 Catholic faithful attended the pontiff's service in Uruguay's western city of Paysandu.

articles.headline: Tech stocks plummet following US midterm election results
articles.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
articles.summary: Major technology firms lost over a trillion dollars in market value after US midterm election results sparked fears of an artificial intelligence development slowdown. Shares in companies like Nvidia and Tesla fell sharply as investors reacted to Democratic campaign promises to restrict data center construction. The Nasdaq composite index has now entered official correction territory.
articles.description: Investors have reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry.

articles.headline: Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight returns to Bengaluru following handwritten hijack threat note
articles.title: Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight returns to Bengaluru after hijack threat note found onboard
articles.summary: An IndiGo flight travelling from Bengaluru to Lucknow made an emergency return to Kempegowda International Airport after cabin crew discovered a handwritten hijack threat note in the lavatory. The aircraft landed safely after fifty-one minutes in the air and underwent thorough inspections by bomb disposal squads and police. Authorities subsequently declared the threat a hoax and launched an investigation to identify who left the note onboard.
articles.description: Flight 6E-451 had departed from Terminal 1 of KIA when cabin crew members found the note that said “This flight is going to hijack at 6.30, ignore and see the consequences”

articles.headline: Police investigate how accused transported seven bodies across locations without detection
articles.title: Rajajingar murders: How did the accused transport bodies across locations without being detected?
articles.summary: Indushekar allegedly transported his wife and six family members in a car across multiple locations including Mysuru and the Tamil Nadu border over a 15-day period without being intercepted by police checkpoints. According to The Hindu, a senior police officer stated that authorities are reviewing patrol negligence and whether the suspect deliberately avoided tolls.
articles.description: Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint detected the accused Indushekhar even as he crossed State borders

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules OBC creamy layer verdict is not retrospective
articles.title: SC clarifies its March 2026 verdict on OBC creamy layer policy will not apply retrospectively
articles.summary: The Supreme Court clarified that its March 2026 judgment regarding OBC non-creamy layer status will not apply retrospectively. The court rejected the government's request for a two-year extension to establish administrative equivalence. The Centre argued that retrospective implementation would cause administrative chaos, affecting past recruitments, seniority, and service allocations across various federal departments.
articles.description: As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment

articles.headline: M Priya stitches costumes for Theyyam performers in male-dominated tradition
articles.title: A woman stitches her way into the male-dominated ritual tradition of Theyyam
articles.summary: M Priya of Kannayi Mukkottu has spent over 15 years specializing in traditional attire for Theyyam performers in Kannur and Kasaragod districts. Learning the craft from her father, she produces specialized garments like kaani and kachunkaraa during the season from November to May. Performers praise her precise stitching, which supports a cultural tradition where women are largely absent.
articles.description: Based in Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur, she spends the Theyyam season creating attire and accessories, a craft she learned from her father and now sustains as a specialised, highly regarded artisan.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court rules Enforcement Directorate is not a super cop
articles.title: Enforcement Directorate is not a ‘super cop’, says Karnataka High Court
articles.summary: The High Court of Karnataka ruled that the Directorate of Enforcement cannot file private complaints to initiate money laundering probes when competent agencies decline scheduled offences. Justice M.I. Arun allowed petitions challenging proceedings initiated by the agency. The court emphasized that enforcement powers are derivative under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and must strictly follow established legal checks and balances.
articles.description: ED cannot file private complaint when other agencies decline to act on its information on alleged offences, court said while quashing ED cases against K.Y. Nanjegowda, Congress MLA from Malur

articles.headline: Manipur inaugurates the Northeast region's first artificial intelligence career intelligence hub
articles.title: Manipur gets Northeast’s first AI-enabled career intelligence hub
articles.summary: Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh inaugurated the artificial intelligence-enabled Career Intelligence Hub at Tamphasana Girls’ Higher Secondary School in Imphal on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Established under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme, the facility aims to provide students with technology-driven career guidance and personalized counselling amidst ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh says the facility marks a significant step towards integrating artificial intelligence into the education and career guidance ecosystem of the State

articles.headline: Nithya Raman wins election to become Los Angeles mayor
articles.title: Nithya Raman | The urban planner
articles.summary: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to become the mayor-elect of Los Angeles. A city council member since 2020 with a background in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Harvard University, Ms. Raman became the first South Asian mayor-elect and the first candidate to defeat a sitting Los Angeles mayor since 2005.
articles.description: Before entering U.S. politics, L.A.’s first South Asian Mayor-elect worked among the urban poor in Chennai, where she used data to expose gaps in slum resettlement and public facilities

articles.headline: East Bengal reaches the AFC Women's Champions League knockout stage despite defeat
articles.title: East Bengal makes history in AFC Women's Champions League
articles.summary: East Bengal FC advanced to the AFC Women’s Champions League quarterfinals on Saturday despite a 2-0 defeat against North Korea’s April 25 SC. Goals from Han Jin-Hong and Oh Sol-Song secured the win for April 25 SC, but the Kolkata side advanced as a top third-placed team by avoiding a defeat by more than three goals.
articles.description: The Kolkata team becomes the first Indian club to advance to the knockout stage of the elite competition

articles.headline: Shreya N. Gowda secures first rank in national defence entrance exam
articles.title: Shreya N. Gowda from Bhadravati tops NDA & NA entrance exam
articles.summary: An engineering student from Bhadravati has achieved the top position among female candidates in the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy examination. The Union Public Service Commission announced the results on November 5, 2026. She will undergo military training in Maharashtra and Uttarakhand. State ministers and local parliamentarians congratulated her on this accomplishment.
articles.description: Shreya N. Gowda of Thimlapura in Bhadravati town has topped the list of women candidates who qualified in the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination conducted by the Union Public Service Commission

articles.headline: Delhi air quality deteriorates to very poor levels with severe pollution spikes
articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi air quality remained in the very poor category with a 24-hour average Air Quality Index of 391 reported by the Central Pollution Control Board on Friday. Several areas across the national capital recorded severe pollution levels, while neighboring towns also experienced poor air. Meteorological factors, stubble burning, and festive activities contributed to the worsening conditions.
articles.description: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Heavy rains flood Gaza
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Heavy rains flood Gaza
articles.description: Jerusalem Daily: Heavy rains flood Gaza

articles.headline: Jon Ossoff wins senate reelection defeating Republican Mike Collins
articles.title: Jon Ossoff | Ambition without ambition
articles.summary: Jon Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, defeating him to defend his Senate seat in Georgia. Mr. Ossoff became the only incumbent Senate Democrat to win in a state won by President Donald Trump in 2024. The 39-year-old senator has faced ongoing media speculation regarding potential 2028 presidential aspirations, which he has vehemently denied.
articles.description: While headlines scream Ossoff looks more presidential after his Senate win, he remains focused on his State while attacking Donald Trump and his family

articles.headline: Heavy rain floods tens of thousands of displaced persons tents in Gaza
articles.title: Heavy rain inundates shelters for people displaced by war in Gaza
articles.summary: Severe downpours on November 7, 2026, inundated roughly seventy thousand tents housing displaced citizens across Gaza, according to local authorities. The flooding caused structural collapses and injuries while overwhelming civil defence teams operating without equipment. Residents and officials appealed for international intervention, emergency shelter, and unrestricted humanitarian aid to prevent further catastrophe amid ongoing military operations.
articles.description: In a statement, the Hamas-run government media office said that about "70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day" of rains

articles.headline: Iraqi prime minister speaks with Trump to avoid regional conflict
articles.title: Iraq’s al-Zaidi talks to Trump as Baghdad seeks to stay out of war on Iran
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi discussed regional security with United States President Donald Trump, stating that Baghdad will not permit its territory to be used for attacks against neighbours. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein warned that a renewed war would be disastrous for Iraq, which has already suffered significant oil revenue losses during the conflict.
articles.description: Call comes as Iraq's top diplomat urges armed groups not to join any Iranian retaliation to US attacks.

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena steps down amid banking crisis
articles.title: Santiago Pena, Paraguay President, steps down as banking crisis sows chaos
articles.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned following the Central Bank seizure of Ueno Bank, which froze deposits for approximately three million people. The November 5, 2026 takeover sparked angry protests, clashes with police, and unanimous parliamentary impeachment proceedings over alleged conflicts of interest. Opposition lawmakers criticized the administration for draining the institution. Vice President Pedro Alliana is scheduled to assume leadership of the South American nation.
articles.description: Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to protest against the President

articles.headline: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticizes central government during Kochi protest
articles.title: CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government
articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar during a demonstration in Kochi on November 7, 2026. Criticizing the Narendra Modi-led administration over alleged electoral irregularities, Mr. Dipke asserted that the government must fall in the 2029 general elections. The event featured addresses by various activists and political figures including actor Prakash Raj.
articles.description: Addressing a protest named ‘Jantar Mantar @ Kochi’ demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Abhijeet Dipke stresses that “Modi will go out in 2029.”

articles.headline: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani reports personal data leak by hackers
articles.title: Italian foreign minister says hackers leaked his personal data
articles.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani announced on social media that cybercriminals published his personal data on the dark web due to his nation's support for Ukraine. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni attributed the incident to pro-Russian hackers, expressing concern over the circulation of confidential institutional information. Mr. Tajani confirmed that the threats also extend to his family members as the government maintains its military and humanitarian backing for Kyiv.
articles.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has blamed pro-Russian hackers for publishing the details online.

articles.headline: Biswajit Basu becomes fourth retired judge to resign from tribunal
articles.title: Biswajit Basu becomes fourth retired judge to resign from West Bengal SIR tribunal
articles.summary: Retired Calcutta High Court judge Biswajit Basu resigned from a Special Intensive Revision tribunal in West Bengal citing personal reasons, making him the fourth former judge to step down. The tribunals were constituted by the Election Commission of India to hear thirty-eight lakh voter appeals following the deletion of ninety-one lakh electors during the revision process held between October 2025 and February 2026.
articles.description: Others who quit are former Calcutta HC Chief Justice T.S. Sivagnanam, former judges Ranjit Kumar Bagh and Indrajit Chatterjee; judges heading the 19 tribunals have complained about the slow pace of disposal of 38 lakh pending appeals

articles.headline: Israeli settlers seize eight Palestinian homes in Jericho amid widespread displacement
articles.title: Israeli settlers seize 8 Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens
articles.summary: United Nations officials condemned an incident where approximately 30 Israeli settlers forcibly took over eight Palestinian homes in the West Bank city of Jericho on Wednesday. According to the UN, the intruders assaulted residents with live ammunition and stones, displacing dozens of families. Meanwhile, regional authorities disputed settler claims that the properties were legally purchased, citing forged documents.
articles.description: UN says settlers reportedly used live ammunition and beat Palestinians, forcing families to flee for their safety.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins US Senate seat in historic midterm election
articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated Republican former Representative Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote to become the first Muslim member of the United States Senate. Published on November 4, 2026, the report notes this victory occurred during the midterm elections alongside Democratic wins in various regions, though analysts emphasized the unique significance of Dr. El-Sayed breaking long-standing political barriers.
articles.description: Abdul El-Sayed’s describes himself as ‘just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works’ and identifies as a progressive; his candidacy was backed by leading figures such as Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister orders relief and price controls after cyclone
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to expedite relief operations following Cyclone Murasu, focusing on power restoration and price regulation of essential commodities. Authorities reported that repair work is underway across 1,825 villages, essential items have been distributed to 3.82 lakh families, and legal action has been taken against 204 traders for violating pricing directives.
articles.description: Naidu tells officials to monitor field-level relief operations, complete damage assessments at the earliest and esnure prompt financial assistance to the affected families

articles.headline: K.C. Venugopal claims Chief Election Commissioner will be forced to step down
articles.title: Gyanesh Kumar will soon be forced to step down, says K.C. Venugopal
articles.summary: All India Congress Committee general secretary K.C. Venugopal accused the leadership of electoral malpractice and stated that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would soon be forced to resign. Speaking at a rally in Kozhikode, Venugopal alleged large-scale vote theft across multiple states and claimed that 13.32 crore voters had been deleted from electoral rolls nationwide.
articles.description: AICC general secretary accuses Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of using the Election Commission of India to undermine the Congress and influence electoral outcomes

articles.headline: Guatemalan congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers killed in attack
articles.title: Guatemalan lawmaker and three police officers killed in armed attack
articles.summary: Congressman Julio Portillo and three National Civil Police officers were killed in an armed assault in Rio Hondo within the Zacapa department, according to Guatemalan authorities. President Bernardo Arevalo instructed security forces to cooperate with prosecutors investigating the incident. The National Unity of Hope party confirmed the death of Portillo, who had previously won his seat for the Cabal party in 2023.
articles.description: It happened in a region of the country known to have drug trafficking activity.

articles.headline: Bengaluru police retrieve two bodies in Rajajinagar murder case
articles.title: Rajajinagar murders: Police retrieve two more bodies from Tamil Nadu; search on for four
articles.summary: Bengaluru police investigating the Rajajinagar murder case retrieved two decomposed bodies from near the Yercaud forest area in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Authorities believe the remains belong to the prime accused Indushekhar's wife Sunita and mother-in-law Roopavathi. Indushekhar was previously arrested for allegedly killing seven family members over eighteen days. Deputy Commissioner of Police B. Nemagoud is leading the ongoing investigation.
articles.description: Teams have been deployed to conduct search operations at Chamundi Hills and Shiradi Ghat as part of the next phase of the investigation to find the missing bodies

articles.headline: Historic Lavi Fair opens in Rampur with traditional trade and culture
articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.summary: The annual Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Himachal Pradesh, runs through November with trading grounds offering textiles, dry fruits, and Chamurthi horses. Originating from a 17th-century treaty, the event generates substantial revenue primarily allocated to local cultural programs. Deputy Commissioner of Police Anupam Kashyap and officials emphasize the fair's enduring role in celebrating Himalayan heritage and supporting small-scale women entrepreneurs.
articles.description: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

articles.headline: Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisis
articles.title: Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisis
articles.description: Lawmakers have voted to impeach Paraguay’s President Santiago Pena amid a banking collapse that has roiled the country.

articles.headline: Health minister announces free Risdiplam distribution for SMA patients in all districts
articles.title: Free Risdiplam for SMA patients to be made available in all districts
articles.summary: The government will make the spinal muscular atrophy medication Risdiplam available through medical colleges in all districts to ease patient distress. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan announced that the Additional Chief Secretary will coordinate the decentralised distribution. Officials are also working to remove the current age restriction of twelve years to benefit all eligible patients across the region.

articles.headline: US government approves Nvidia chip sales to empty office in China
articles.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
articles.summary: Concerns have emerged regarding the vetting process after the United States Commerce Department approved Nvidia chip sales to a Chinese firm named New Matrix, which operates out of an empty office. According to The New York Times, the company's owners have ties to a blacklisted private equity firm. The Trump administration previously relaxed chip sales limits following an agreement involving revenue sharing and lobbying efforts.
articles.description: Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company's H200 AI chips. According to The New York Times, New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, "a hollow gray shell […]

articles.headline: Iran constructs underground military complexes for weapons production and storage
articles.title: Iran’s IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage
articles.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced the construction of underground military complexes designed to maintain weapons manufacturing and storage during heavy bombardments. Speaking in Tehran, spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi highlighted advancements in stealth technology and missile capabilities. Meanwhile, the United States military launched limited strikes on Qeshm Island as diplomatic and economic tensions between the nations persist.
articles.description: IRGC says underground military complexes allow missile production to continue even under heavy bombardment.

articles.headline: Trump’s new chief of staff Stephen Miller says he ‘saved America’
articles.title: Trump’s new chief of staff Stephen Miller says he ‘saved America’
articles.description: Stephen Miller, US President Donald Trump’s incoming chief of staff praises him.

articles.headline: Michel Barnier warns United Kingdom cannot cherry pick single market access
articles.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
articles.summary: The European Union's former Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier stated that the United Kingdom cannot selectively access the single market without accepting all four freedoms, including the free movement of people. Speaking to the BBC, Barnier asserted that any UK return to the internal market would require adherence to standard bloc conditions and rejected the possibility of reinstating a British financial rebate.
articles.description: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".

articles.headline: Telangana Women's Commission questions inaction over illegal oocyte racket
articles.title: Agents booked, five fertility centres named in Hyderabad’s illegal oocyte racket; Telangana Women’s Commission questions inaction
articles.summary: The Telangana Women's Commission has questioned authorities regarding the lack of legal action against five fertility centres allegedly involved in an illegal egg collection racket in Hyderabad. Forty-three vulnerable women were rescued after being offered between twenty thousand and thirty thousand rupees per cycle, while operators made about three lakh rupees per cycle. Commission Chairperson Nerella Sharada identified the implicated institutions as Indira IVF Centre, Narmada Fertility Centre, Oasis Fertility Centre, Sadguru ART Centre, and Padmaja Fertility Centre, and demanded immediate inquiries and strict legal measures.

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet approves Bill to establish Sannati development authority
articles.title: Sannati set for a heritage makeover as Karnataka Cabinet clears development authority Bill
