articles.description: The midterms showed that challenging support for Israel can win votes. But changing US foreign policy may be harder.

articles.headline: Joint List alliance to support Gadi Eisenkot for Israeli premiership
articles.title: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government
articles.summary: The Joint List, an alliance of Arab-led parties, announced Thursday it will recommend opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form Israel's next government. With the support of the Ra'am party, Eisenkot is expected to secure 67 seats in the Knesset. President Isaac Herzog is currently consulting with party leaders to determine who will be tasked with forming a coalition.
articles.description: Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel's 120-seat parliament in last week's general election.

articles.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to ten years in prison under Hong Kong security law
articles.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
articles.summary: Pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to ten years in prison on November 5, 2026, for colluding with foreign forces under Hong Kong's national security law. Having already spent six years behind bars for previous convictions, the thirty-year-old co-founder of the defunct political party Demosisto received the latest sentence after pleading guilty in September to charges related to lobbying foreign governments.
articles.description: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.

articles.headline: What can Democrats do in Congress under President Trump?
articles.title: What can Democrats do in Congress under President Trump?
articles.description: What can the Democratic party actually change when it comes to Donald Trump’s decisions, policies and presidency?

articles.headline: Indonesia rushes thousands of troops to Jakarta amid wiretap scandal
articles.title: Indonesia rushes thousands of troops to Jakarta amid wiretap scandal
articles.description: Indonesia is deploying thousands of troops in Jakarta amid an alleged wiretapping scandal targeting the president.

articles.headline: European Union prosecutors launch probe into Spanish rail network financing fraud
articles.title: EU prosecutor office investigates fatal train crash in Spain
articles.summary: European Union public prosecutors initiated an investigation into potential financing fraud regarding Spain's high-speed rail network following a fatal train crash in Urda that killed 69 passengers. The European Public Prosecutor's Office conducted investigative measures at three Spanish infrastructure organisations. The collision followed a previous crash in January and preceded the resignations of Transport Minister Oscar Puente and rail manager president Luis Pedro Marco de la Pena.
articles.description: The EU office carries out probes at Spanish rail network administrator, safety agency and state auditors.

articles.headline: Somalian tour guide changes global perceptions of Mogadishu through local tourism
articles.title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
articles.summary: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader works as a local tour guide in Mogadishu, showing international visitors beaches, historic sites and markets to counter negative media stereotypes of conflict. According to the country's tourism department, ten thousand tourists visited Somalia in 2024, representing a fifty percent increase from the previous year. Foreign travellers say the welcoming atmosphere and coastal scenery starkly contrast with ongoing security challenges.
articles.description: For some tourists, the contrast between Somalia's reputation and what they experience on the ground can be striking.

articles.headline: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to approach courts regarding residence threats
articles.title: Zubeen Garg case: Assam CM flags danger to family in threat to besiege his house
articles.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced on November 6, 2026, that the state government will notify the Supreme Court and Gauhati High Court regarding threats from a group led by an MLA to gherao his residence. The group warned of protests if bail is granted to prime accused Shyamkanu Mahanta and Siddhartha Sharma in the Zubeen Garg death case, which Sarma condemned as a direct danger to his family.
articles.description: He told journalists in Guwahati that he would bring the threat to the notice of the Supreme Court and the Gauhati High Court, as it could amount to an attempt to murder

articles.headline: Israeli military strikes in Gaza kill four Palestinians
articles.title: Four people, including a child, killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
articles.summary: At least four Palestinians, including a child, were killed in Israeli drone and artillery strikes across central and southern Gaza on Thursday. Medical sources reported casualties in Deir el-Balah, Khan Younis, and Bureij refugee camp. According to the Gaza Health Ministry, the total death toll in the enclave has reached 74,618 since the conflict began in 2023.
articles.description: Gaza officials say more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called 'ceasefire' took effect.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV arrives for South American tour after cancer surgery
articles.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives for South American tour after cancer surgery
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Uruguay kicking off a 12-day tour of South America after undergoing lung surgery last month.

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football.

articles.headline: Adani Ports to acquire European liquid storage operator Evos for 2.56 billion euros
articles.title: Adani Ports to acquire Europe’s Evos for €2.56 billion EV
articles.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd (APSEZ) will purchase the Netherlands-based Evos B.V. from Igneo Infrastructure Partners in an all-cash deal. The acquisition, valued at 2.56 billion euros, provides APSEZ with eight terminals across Europe. This move marks the company's entry into the global liquid storage market, supporting its goal of handling one billion tonnes.
articles.description: The terminals are strategically located in major European energy and industrial hubs, including the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) region, Hamburg and the Mediterranean.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets rally as Sensex jumps over 2,000 points
articles.title: Markets surge for sixth day; Sensex jumps 2,009 points
articles.summary: The BSE Sensex surged 2,009 points to close at 79,310 on November 5, 2026, marking a six-day winning streak. The NSE Nifty also climbed 576 points. Investors were encouraged by falling crude oil prices and the Democratic Party's victory in the U.S. midterm elections, which saw them gain control of both the Senate and the House.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex zoomed 2,008.61 points, or 2.60%, to settle at 79,310.01, and the 50-share NSE Nifty surged 576 points, or 2.40%, to end at 24,536.60

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
articles.title: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
articles.summary: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international duty after a 23-year career. The 41-year-old, who debuted in 2003, holds world records with 234 caps and 146 goals. His decision follows a recent departure from the national team camp after being excluded from the starting lineup for a Nations League match against Denmark.
articles.description: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".

articles.headline: MTG warns Miller-Wiles shakeup will sink Republican chances in 2028
articles.title: MTG warns Miller-Wiles shakeup will sink Republican chances in 2028
articles.description: Marjorie Taylor Greene says Trump's White House personnel shuffle will sink the party’s next presidential campaign.

articles.headline: Workers strike across France as protests expand to hundreds of cities
articles.title: Workers strike across France, hundreds of thousands expected to protest
articles.summary: Workers across France have launched nationwide strikes to demand higher wages, tax reforms, and improved public services. Demonstrations occurred in 260 cities, including Paris and Marseille, following student-led protests that began in September. President Emmanuel Macron convened a security meeting as unions and teachers pushed for change ahead of the upcoming presidential election in April.
articles.description: Demonstrators are demanding an increase in the minimum wage and higher salaries for all workers, among other reforms.

articles.headline: New Zealanders vote in general election amid economic concerns
articles.title: New Zealanders vote in tightly contested general election
articles.summary: Polling stations opened across New Zealand on the final day of voting in a tightly contested general election dominated by economic concerns and the cost of living. The Electoral Commission reported that more than 1.6 million voters cast ballots prior to the final day, with preliminary results expected following the closure of polling places.
articles.description: More than half of New Zealand’s voters cast early ballots in the tightly contested race.

articles.headline: Cornell faculty passes no confidence vote over leadership handling sexual assault allegations
articles.title: Cornell faculty pass no-confidence vote over leadership's handling of Jane Doe allegations
articles.summary: Academic staff at Cornell University passed a symbolic no-confidence vote against central administrators regarding their response to a former student's gang rape allegations involving the Chi Phi fraternity. President Michael Kotlikoff faces criticism over the institution's handling of the case, though the board of trustees maintains support. Meanwhile, New York state prosecutors and state police are conducting separate investigations into the matter.
articles.description: Friday's resolution by academic staff is largely symbolic as they do not have the power to remove those in charge of the university.

articles.headline: U.S. midterm elections feature historic firsts for governors and senators
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
articles.summary: Voters across the United States elected several groundbreaking candidates during the November 3, 2026, midterm elections. Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia as the first Black female governor, Deb Haaland became New Mexico's first Native American female governor, Abdul El-Sayed won a Senate seat in Michigan as the first Muslim senator, Chris Pappas became the first openly gay male senator in New Hampshire, and Peggy Flanagan secured a Senate seat as the first Native American female senator.
articles.description: The US midterm elections delivered a series of historic firsts by electing a Black female governor, a Muslim senator and openly gay male US senator

articles.headline: Ukraine shares battlefield data with US software firm Palantir
articles.title: Palantir harvests battlefield data that Ukraine pays for ‘with blood’
articles.summary: Ukraine is collaborating with the Florida-based software company Palantir to collect battlefield data for training military artificial intelligence. While the government views the partnership as a strategic asset, some officials have questioned the ethics of sharing sensitive combat information with a private firm. Palantir maintains that customers retain full control over their own data sets.
articles.description: The US company is using Kyiv’s unique war data to train its controversial technologies.

articles.headline: Republican lawmakers consider impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title: ‘Knives out’: Will Congress impeach Pete Hegseth after GOP midterms loss?
articles.summary: Following significant losses in the US midterm elections, Republican lawmakers are discussing the potential impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Critics, including Congressman Thomas Massie, blame Hegseth for the unpopular war in Iran and allege constitutional violations. While President Donald Trump continues to support his defense chief, pressure for a resignation is mounting within the party.
articles.description: Democrats can adopt the impeachment articles in the House but will need Republican backing in the Senate.

articles.headline: Democrats win control of Congress following US midterm elections
articles.title: Iran, Gaza, Ukraine: What will US midterm results mean for these conflicts?
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate during this week's midterm elections. The results are widely seen as a referendum on President Donald Trump’s policies, particularly the ongoing war in Iran. Lawmakers now face questions regarding how they will address conflicts in Iran, Gaza, and Ukraine starting in January.
articles.description: Despite wins, Democrats lack the two-thirds majority needed to overturn a presidential veto and push through a law.

articles.headline: Democrats win congressional majorities following voter backlash against Donald Trump
articles.title: Democrats vow to rein in Donald Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
articles.summary: Following voter anger over living costs and the United States-Iran war, Democrats secured majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives during the November 2026 midterm elections. The historic defeat marks the first time President Donald Trump will face opposition control in both congressional chambers, potentially leading to legislative deadlock and investigations into his administration, while Republican leaders and Vice President J.D. Vance acknowledged the war played a role in the losses.
articles.description: It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress

articles.headline: India extends five hundred million dollar credit line to Guyana
articles.title: India announces extension of $500 million line of credit for Guyana
articles.summary: During the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar announced an extension of a five hundred million dollar line of credit to Guyana for infrastructure, health, and defense projects. Meeting with Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on Wednesday, Jaishankar also oversaw the signing of three bilateral agreements regarding small enterprises, quick impact projects, and digital public infrastructure cooperation.
articles.description: EAM Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting

articles.headline: Vice President J D Vance blames administration policies for Republican midterm rout
articles.title: Vance eyes own trail in America First politics in Republican rout
articles.summary: United States Vice President J.D. Vance stated that the administration, rather than the electorate, abandoned America First principles and caused the Republican midterm election losses. Highlighting the war on Iran as a primary factor, Mr. Vance's public disavowal strengthens his position as a potential presidential contender for two thousand twenty-eight while distancing him from Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
articles.description: What continues to work for Mr. Vance is that he manages to challenge and critique Mr. Trump without triggering a meltdown from the latter. Whether he can continue in that manner all the way to the 2028 election remains to be seen. But Mr. Vance would be perfectly capable of carrying forward his own version of America First without Mr. Trump

articles.headline: Donald Trump struggles to control narrative following US midterms defeat
articles.title: How Trump’s unconvincing narrative on Iran lost him the US midterms
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump faced significant political fallout following a historic defeat for Republicans in the most expensive election in American history. Contributors analyzed the Democratic sweep, media changes in Serbia involving Aleksandar Vucic, and the launch of Equator magazine by former mainstream media journalists during discussions on global politics.
articles.description: Donald Trump and the Republicans struggle to spin a historic defeat in the US midterms.

articles.headline: Big Tech companies continue record spending on AI infrastructure
articles.title: Big Tech’s big AI buildout will not end until someone stops it
articles.summary: Major technology firms including Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta plan to spend at least $720 billion on capital expenditures this year, primarily for AI data centers. Despite this massive investment, companies have yet to see significant financial returns. Investors are increasingly concerned as revenue growth in core businesses is being impacted by these AI-focused initiatives.
articles.description: After four of the biggest competitors in the AI race held quarterly earnings calls late last month, two things are clear: Big Tech is not done spending record amounts on the AI data center buildout, and the AI data center buildout is not any closer to yielding its promised returns. A third thing is also […]

articles.headline: Displaced families in Gaza face winter in hazardous coastal tents
articles.title: ‘Helpless’: The families facing winter in tents on the beach in Gaza
articles.summary: Displaced families in Gaza are struggling to survive in dilapidated tents along the coastline as winter approaches. Many residents, forced from their homes, face risks from flooding, cold, and wind. Aid groups are attempting to mitigate the danger by using repurposed cooking pots filled with soil to create barriers against encroaching seawater and winter storms.
articles.description: An innovative idea to turn damaged cooking pots into seawater barriers is providing families in Gaza with some relief.

articles.headline: Republican allies distance themselves from Iran war following election defeat
articles.title: Congress defeat: How Trump’s allies are distancing themselves from Iran war
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance and other Republican allies are distancing themselves from the ongoing war in Iran after the party's midterm election losses. While President Donald Trump maintains the conflict was necessary, critics argue the war's political and economic costs contributed to the defeat. Democrats now plan to use congressional funding powers to challenge the administration.
articles.description: US Vice President JD Vance blames the war for the midterm rout as Democrats prepare to use Congress to rein it in.

articles.headline: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq placed under house detention and barred from prayers
articles.title: Disallowed Friday prayers, under house detention for 6th day: Mirwaiz
articles.summary: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq stated that authorities prevented him from leading Friday prayers at Jama Masjid in Srinagar for the second consecutive week. Placed under house detention with heavy police barricades outside his residence in the Nigeen area, the religious leader denounced the restrictions as arbitrary measures intended to suppress freedom of expression and contradict official claims of regional normalcy following his previous sermon.
articles.description: On the previous Friday, the Mirwaiz mentioned in his sermon the findings of the International Crisis Group report on Jammu and Kashmir and highlighted the concerns over political prisoners, civil liberties and the need for meaningful political engagement and reconciliation

articles.headline: Yemen government offensive against Houthi forces continues as war of attrition
articles.title: A month after Yemen government offensive began, war of attrition takes hold
articles.summary: A month after the Yemeni government launched Operation Dawn of Yemen to reclaim territory from Houthi fighters, the conflict has settled into a prolonged war of attrition. While the capital Sanaa remains relatively calm, fighting persists in southern provinces. Experts suggest the offensive is straining Houthi supply lines and tribal support, though no decisive victory has emerged.
articles.description: The Houthis suffer losses but also inflict pain on government forces and Saudi Arabia.

articles.headline: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms for supporting Iranian oil exports
articles.title: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms accused of helping Iran
articles.summary: The United States Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkiye for allegedly facilitating Iranian oil exports and supporting sanctioned airlines. The measures target a network accused of using fake maritime certifications. These actions are part of the Trump administration’s campaign to restrict revenue used by Iran for military efforts.
articles.description: US Treasury says Indian couple faked ship registries for countries including Guyana and Laos to help Iranian tankers.

articles.headline: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Texas factory
articles.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
articles.summary: Tesla plans to wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year to focus on self-driving Cybercab cars, according to Elon Musk. Lead engineer Wes Morrill suggested the vehicle is being discontinued. Launched in 2023 following numerous delays and a famous glass-shattering demonstration, the angular truck experienced disappointing sales and several safety recalls.
articles.description: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.

articles.headline: Palestinian couples tie the knot in mass wedding in Gaza
articles.title: Palestinian couples tie the knot in mass wedding in Gaza
articles.description: The event brought 250 couples together to celebrate love and new beginnings despite Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine exchange drone strikes on energy and logistics infrastructure
articles.title: Russia says it hit Ukrainian postal hub and ship as Ukraine strikes Ryazan
articles.summary: Russia and Ukraine traded drone attacks on Thursday, targeting critical infrastructure on both sides. Moscow reported strikes on a Ukrainian postal hub and a cargo ship, while Ukrainian drones ignited fires at an industrial zone in Ryazan, Russia. The ongoing conflict has caused injuries and power outages, with both nations intensifying efforts to disrupt the other's logistics.
articles.description: Injuries reported on both sides as Russia and Ukraine trade overnight drone strikes on energy and logistics sites.

articles.headline: Technology shares recover after massive market sell-off wiped trillions in value
articles.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
articles.summary: Global technology companies experienced a recovery in early trading after a severe market rout began in the United States and spread to Asian and European exchanges. The rebound followed the release of unexpected US employment data showing the economy added 165000 jobs in October alongside a slight decline in the unemployment rate to 41% according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
articles.description: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

articles.headline: Dutch protesters occupy Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam
articles.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam
articles.summary: Demonstrators breached the Amsterdam construction perimeter on Friday to halt infrastructure expansion, leading to between 150 and 200 arrests by law enforcement. Activists from the Geef Tegengas group and pro-Palestinian factions opposed the facility over environmental and surveillance concerns. Similar demonstrations occurred across multiple European nations as grassroots movements challenge the rapid development of digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence workloads.
articles.description: Data centres face protests across Europe due to the massive amounts of computing power and water they use.

articles.headline: Thomas Markle Sr arrested in the US over child abuse material
articles.title: Meghan Markle’s father arrested in US over alleged child sex abuse photos
articles.summary: Thomas Markle Sr, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, was arrested in Florida following the discovery of sexually explicit photographs involving underage girls in two Los Angeles area storage units. The Department of Justice announced the arrest, noting he faces up to twenty years in prison if convicted on federal charges.
articles.description: US authorities found sexually explicit photos that appeared to show Thomas Markle with prepubescent girls.

articles.headline: Migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands after being rescued at sea
articles.title: Migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands after being rescued at sea
articles.description: More than 3,200 migrants were rescued in the first six days of November in Canary Islands, Spain.

articles.headline: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay to begin South American tour
articles.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Uruguay starting 12-day Latin America tour
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Montevideo to launch a twelve-day tour of South America, marking his first major international trip since undergoing lung cancer surgery in October. The seventy-one-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, engaging with local communities and addressing regional challenges despite prior doubts regarding his travel fitness.
articles.description: The pontiff praises Uruguay's clean energy transition and calls for universal healthcare.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules temporary cultivators ineligible for forest rights protection
articles.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that individuals with temporary residence or living outside forest boundaries cannot claim traditional dweller status solely through silk cotton cultivation in the Agasthyamalai biosphere. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta mandated strict adherence to eviction plans while questioning the commercial nature of the agricultural activities.

articles.headline: How ‘Street Medics’ protect French protesters
articles.title: How ‘Street Medics’ protect French protesters
articles.description: French authorities are investigating more than a hundred cases of alleged police misconduct at cost of living protests.

articles.headline: North Korea signals reluctance for summit with U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.title: Donald Trump’s midterm defeat dims hopes of North Korea meeting
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, indicated Pyongyang has no interest in further dialogue with Washington, citing hostility. Analysts suggest the North Korean regime is prioritizing its nuclear arsenal and economic ties with Russia following Donald Trump’s midterm election defeat, which has left the U.S. president with limited political leverage.
articles.description: Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”

articles.headline: Renowned climate scientist P.V. Joseph passes away at age ninety-four
articles.title: Climate scientist P.V. Joseph passes away
articles.summary: Climate scientist P.V. Joseph passed away at age ninety-four. He joined the India Meteorological Department in 1957, later directing its training school and serving as professor at Cochin University of Science and Technology. He discovered the low-level monsoon jetstream, published around 70 research articles, and received several awards including the Sir Gilbert Walker Gold Medal in 2021.
articles.description: He discovered the low-level monsoon jetstream and conducted extensive research on monsoon onset, Rossby waves, and ocean-atmosphere instability

articles.headline: Amazon rainforest now releases more carbon dioxide than it absorbs
articles.title: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter
articles.summary: A study conducted between 2010 and 2024 reveals that the Amazon rainforest has transitioned from a carbon sink into a net carbon source. Researchers using airplanes to measure atmospheric CO2 levels found that deforestation and forest fires have decimated the region's capacity to offset human-induced emissions, rendering the forest unable to mitigate regional anthropogenic pollution levels.
articles.description: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon.

articles.headline: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister welcomes Supreme Court power arrears verdict
articles.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
articles.summary: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu hailed a Supreme Court directive ordering Punjab and Haryana to supply nearly twelve thousand million units of electricity over twenty years as a historic victory. The ruling resolves a decades-old dispute over hydroelectric project shares, providing substantial projected revenue to bolster state infrastructure and public services.
articles.description: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects

articles.headline: Hong Kong court sentences pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten additional years
articles.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail
articles.summary: Hong Kong High Court Judge William Tam sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten additional years in prison after finding him guilty of colluding with foreign entities under the national security law. Wong, who pleaded guilty in September, was already serving time for previous protest-related offenses and faced condemnation from foreign governments and rights organizations including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch following the ruling.
articles.description: Wong, in prison since 2020, was found guilty of colluding with foreign entities in violation of national security law.

articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections determining presidential power
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
articles.summary: Americans went to the polls on November 3, 2026, in midterm elections that will determine how much power United States President Donald Trump retains for the remainder of his term. Voters decided all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats, and 36 state governorships. Over 210 million registered citizens were eligible to cast ballots across the country as voting concluded.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states went for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote

articles.headline: Kerala High Court criticises Kochi Corporation over unmaintained footpaths
articles.title: Pedestrian’s death: Kerala HC raps Kochi Corpn. over alleged failure to restore footpaths in city
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court criticised the Kochi Corporation regarding unmaintained footpaths following a private bus accident in Kakkanad that caused a 28-year-old woman's death. The court instructed authorities to ensure pedestrian safety and strict action against overspeeding buses. Deputy Commissioner of Police Arun K. Pavithran reported that employee details are being recorded through a Smart ID system and complaint numbers will be displayed on vehicles.
articles.description: Court observes that the woman killed in the Kakkanad accident had no space to move aside to avoid the oncoming bus, and reiterates that the right to pedestrian paths is a fundamental right

articles.headline: Tanzanian opposition leader jailed in ‘politically motivated’ case
articles.title: Tanzanian opposition leader jailed in ‘politically motivated’ case
articles.description: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu has been jailed in a case widely condemned as politically motivated.

articles.headline: Global emissions remain high as Paris Agreement marks ten years
articles.title: Ten years of the Paris Agreement: Has the world kept its climate promises?
articles.summary: Celebrating ten years since its entry into force, the Paris Agreement has successfully driven clean energy expansion, though global greenhouse gas emissions remain near record highs and scientists warn that the one point five degree Celsius warming limit will likely be surpassed soon. China, the United States, and India continue to produce over half of annual emissions, and despite national climate policies reducing projections to about two point six degrees of warming by twenty one hundred, current reductions remain too slow.
articles.description: Nearly 200 countries pledged to limit warming to 1.5C. We look at who has delivered and who has fallen short.

articles.headline: Why is Britain refusing to pay slavery reparations?
articles.title: Why is Britain refusing to pay slavery reparations?
articles.description: Britain compensated slave owners, not the enslaved. Can an apology without reparations be enough?

articles.headline: Supreme Court bans illegal detentions and orders normal transit operations in Delhi
articles.title: Supreme Court bars illegal detention as lawyers cite Emergency
articles.summary: During an extraordinary Sunday hearing, Supreme Court Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ordered the Union government and the Delhi Police to halt illegal detentions and restore normal public transport, internet access, and movement around Delhi following a massive security clampdown. Senior lawyers compared the police actions to the nineteen seventy-five Emergency, while Solicitor General Tushar Mehta defended the government actions and agreed to file an affidavit addressing the restrictions.
articles.description: Court seeks affidavits on Metro curbs and alleged violations of its October 9 order

articles.headline: Telangana introduces climate resilience plan featuring cool roofs and bamboo shelters
articles.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
articles.summary: Telangana is implementing a comprehensive climate action plan to build urban resilience against rising temperatures and extreme weather through a project pipeline worth twenty thousand crore rupees. According to municipal officials, the long-term vision incorporates mandatory urban road codes, cool roof policies, and extensive waste bio-mining programmes designed to reduce emissions, reclaim land, and expand wastewater treatment across local bodies by 2047.
articles.description: The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. The plan, which also includes waste reclamation, sewage treatment and digital monitoring of water supply, seeks to build climate resilience across urban local bodies

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu political leaders demand investigation into library book procurement fraud
articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: political leaders raise concern over allegations, call for action
articles.summary: Prominent political figures in Tamil Nadu have expressed serious concern and called for immediate investigations following allegations by writer Perumal Murugan regarding fraudulent book procurements at the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam public library in Coimbatore. Leaders urged authorities to audit all library materials, remove artificially generated books, and investigate suspicious publishing houses involved in supplying the institution.
articles.description: Kamal Haasan demands the immediate withdrawal of the fake books from all libraries. M.H. Jawahirullah wants the formation of an independent committee to examine all books procured for the public library. Others, including Anbumani Ramadoss and K. Annamalai, want the government to take up a thorough investigation of the allegations

articles.headline: Israeli forces close Hebron mosque to Palestinians for Jewish religious holiday
articles.title: Israel closes Hebron’s Ibrahimi Mosque to Palestinians for Jewish holiday
articles.summary: Israeli authorities closed the Ibrahimi Mosque in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinian worshippers to accommodate thousands of Israeli settlers arriving for an annual holiday commemorating Sarah. According to the Palestinian Ministry of Religious Endowments, employees were barred and the call to prayer was suspended while security forces tightened movement restrictions throughout the Old City.
articles.description: Contested West Bank holy site is reopened exclusively for Israelis, deepening tensions over control of the mosque.

articles.headline: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian player in Youth Olympic badminton final
articles.title: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian badminton player to reach Youth Olympic badminton final
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri from Odisha made history by defeating Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe twenty-one to fourteen, eleven to twenty-one, and twenty-one to nineteen during a fifty-four minute semifinal. The victory makes her the first Indian badminton player to reach the women's singles final at the Youth Olympic Games, where she will face China's Yi Xin Zhang for the gold medal.
articles.description: The 15-year-old from Odisha continued her impressive run, stunning Japan’s second seed, Yuzuno Watanabe, 21-14, 11-21, 21-19, in a hard-fought 54-minute semifinal to book her place in the title clash

articles.headline: Markets surge on falling oil prices and United States midterm election results
articles.title: Markets on spree after crude tumbles 9% following Trump’s midterm fallout
articles.summary: Stock market indices Sensex and Nifty recorded sharp gains in early trading on November 5, 2026, driven by a ten percent drop in crude oil prices and investor optimism following the United States midterm elections. American voters handed control of Congress to the Democratic Party, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the West Asia conflict and easing inflationary pressures across international markets.
articles.description: Analysts suggest that the sharp decline in oil prices and the opening up of the Strait of Hormuz are anchoring the Indian markets

articles.headline: Paraguay faces political crisis and impeachment proceedings following digital lender collapse
articles.title: Why is Paraguay facing a banking and political crisis?
articles.summary: Paraguay is experiencing severe political turmoil following the collapse of the digital lender Ueno, which prevented millions of customers from accessing their savings and triggered intense scrutiny of major state institutions. The national congress rejected the resignation of President Santiago Pena and advanced impeachment proceedings against him, alleging negligence and complicity in covering up the financial insolvency of the bank.
articles.description: Ueno collapse raises questions about state influence and accountability.

articles.headline: Fast bowlers face physical compromises and format shifts with age
articles.title: Still searing: how outlier Starc has kept the fire burning
articles.summary: The article discusses the physical challenges faced by fast bowlers as they age in professional cricket. It highlights how many players reduce their velocity or transition exclusively to white-ball formats to avoid the physical demands associated with five-day Test matches. The text does not provide specific names, dates, or additional outcomes regarding any individual athlete.
articles.description: The rangy left-armer is bowling better than ever at 36, operating at rapid speeds and expanding his repertoire. In an era when his unique skill-set warrants big money from T20 leagues around the world, he has gone against the grain: he has preserved himself for Test cricket.

articles.headline: Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint over false Form 7s
articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing
articles.summary: The Electoral Registration Officer of Mustafabad lodged a police complaint seeking an FIR under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act. North East District Election Officer Ajay Kumar stated that officials verified reports and found 36 out of 37 voter deletion forms to be fabricated. The investigation into additional applications remains ongoing across the constituency area.
articles.description: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

articles.headline: Madurai police arrest former deputy mayor over horse-trading allegations
articles.title: TVK MLA’s ‘horse trading’ claim: former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan arrested, released on bail
articles.summary: Madurai City Police arrested former Madurai Corporation Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan on November 6, 2026, following allegations of bribery by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA V.M.S. Mustafa. Mr. Mannan was produced before a special court and released on bail. Opposition leaders Edappadi K. Palaniswami and T.T.V. Dhinakaran condemned the arrest, criticizing the ruling government for alleged political targeting.
articles.description: Based on Madurai Central TVK MLA Mustafa’s complaint of horse-trading bid, CCB registers case under Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and for criminal conspiracy and Mr. Mannan, now with the AIADMK, was picked up for inquiry.

articles.headline: DMK demands independent probe into Periyar Arivulagam book procurement
articles.title: DMK demands independent probe into book procurement for Periyar Arivulagam
articles.summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam demanded an independent investigation on November 6, 2026, into alleged irregularities involving book procurement for the Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore. Former Higher Education Minister Govi. Chezhiaan called for transparency and legal action against those responsible, while questioning the motives of the current administration under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.
articles.description: Former Higher Education Minister Govi. Chezhiaan issues statement after Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay blames the erstwhile DMK government for the issue

articles.headline: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey calls for reclaiming parts of Bangladesh
articles.title: Time has come to ‘reclaim’ Noakhali, Chittagong and Sylhet: Nishikant Dubey
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Member of Parliament Nishikant Dubey stated on November 6, 2026, that India should reclaim Noakhali, Chittagong, and Sylhet from Bangladesh. Mr. Dubey blamed former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru for ceding these territories during Partition. The remarks received support from Pradyot Manikya, head of the Tipra Motha party and a descendant of Tripura's last king.
articles.description: The BJP MP blames Jawaharlal Nehru saying he wanted the support of Muslim League in the interim government of 1946 when the decision was taken to leave these three regions for East Pakistan

articles.headline: ‘Message to the West’ bomb threats target European newsrooms, travel
articles.title: ‘Message to the West’ bomb threats target European newsrooms, travel
articles.description: Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received bomb threats from someone identifying themself as ‘Mikhail Andropov’.

articles.headline: President Donald Trump halts military aid to Israel amid midterm fallout
articles.title: Midterm results put U.S.-Israel ties under further strain
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on election day that Washington will end approximately four billion dollars in annual military aid to Israel by the end of the year. Citing political costs and the success of Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, the decision places additional strain on diplomatic relations between the two long-standing allies in West Asia.
articles.description: Critics on both sides argue that Mr. Netanyahu pulled Mr. Trump into a war he could not win. Now when even the Vice-President is blaming the war for the electoral defeat, the real target is the ‘special relationship’ with Israel

articles.headline: BJP booth level agents deny filing voter deletion forms in Mustafabad
articles.title: Who filed 77% of Form 7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad? BJP BLAs named as ‘objectors’ deny them
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party booth level agents named as objectors in seventy-seven percent of deletion applications in Delhi’s Mustafabad constituency denied association with the filings. The Hindu reported that sixteen of twenty registered agents denied submitting Form seven applications targeting Muslim electors since August thirty-first, two thousand twenty-six. The applications allegedly violated an Election Commission of India cap introduced on October ninth, two thousand twenty-six.
articles.description: Of the 20 BJP-appointed Booth Level Agents named in 787 deletion applications, 16 deny submitting or signing the forms, while one says he filed “over 500”

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government disbands high-level committee on union-state relations
articles.title: T.N. govt. disbands High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government disbanded the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations on November 6, 2026, transferring its mandate to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission. Formed in April 2025 under former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and chaired by retired Supreme Court Judge Kurian Joseph, the non-statutory panel was dissolved because its functions overlapped with the State Law Commission.
articles.description: Its mandate has been transferred to the State Law Commission, according to a Government Order issued on November 6, 2026

articles.headline: ONGC Videsh expects to secure Venezuelan oil project operatorship soon
articles.title: ONGC expects to acquire operatorship rights in Venezuelan oil projects in 3-6 months’ time
articles.summary: The overseas arm of India's Oil and Natural Gas Company (ONGC) expects to finalise operatorship of Venezuela's San Cristobal and Carabobo oil projects within three to six months. Director Anupam Agarwal stated this shift will allow the firm to recoup over $500 million in stuck dividends by gaining direct control over crude oil offtake rights.
articles.description: ONGC holds 40% interest in Venezuela’s San Cristobal oil project and 11% stake in Carabobo project.

articles.headline: Indian government overhauls Agnipath recruitment scheme with extended service options
articles.title: What are the changes in Agniveer scheme, and what prompted government to implement them? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indian Cabinet approved a major overhaul of the Agnipath recruitment scheme on November 4, 2026. Based on recommendations from the three armed services, the policy grants Agniveers not initially selected for regular service an additional two years of engagement, establishing a clear pathway for all willing personnel to eventually join the military as regular soldiers.
articles.description: The decision, approved by the Cabinet on the recommendations of the three services, creates a pathway for the eventual absorption of all willing Agniveers, subject to merit and prescribed selection criteria

articles.headline: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens
articles.title: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens
articles.description: Israeli settlers have forced dozens of Palestinians from their homes in Jericho after seizing eight properties.

articles.headline: Myanmar military plans byelections for April 2027 in 39 constituencies
articles.title: Myanmar to conduct byelections next April
articles.summary: The Union Election Commission announced that byelections will take place on April 4, 2027, across 39 parliamentary constituencies in Myanmar. The scheduled vote covers areas where previous polling was restricted due to ongoing civil conflict since the 2021 military coup led by Min Aung Hlaing, as well as seats vacated by promoted lawmakers. Conflict monitors estimate the civil war has claimed over 100000 lives.
articles.description: The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives

articles.headline: CERT-In releases security guidelines for auditing autonomous artificial intelligence agents
articles.title: CERT-In calls for testing AI agents for unauthorised tool use, privilege abuse
articles.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team issued new auditing guidelines on November 5, 2026, to secure advanced artificial intelligence systems capable of autonomous tasks and tool use. The framework mandates rigorous testing for unauthorised permission usage, privilege abuse, credential misuse, memory manipulation, and multi-agent communication risks to ensure strict operational safety and accountability within production environments.
articles.description: Guidelines require checks on agents’ permissions, task delegation and emergency-stop mechanisms; multi-agent systems must maintain authenticated, logged communications and records of actions

articles.headline: Meta introduces custom interactive spaces within its Muse artificial intelligence assistant
articles.title: Meta’s Muse AI can create custom ‘spaces’ for the version of the app you need right now
articles.summary: Meta Platforms is rolling out customizable spaces inside its Muse artificial intelligence assistant, enabling users to build features like shopping hubs and school dashboards. According to the company, users can create these experiences through natural language descriptions and connect them to relevant applications for background updates. The company is also testing ways to share and collaborate on spaces with other users.
articles.description: Meta will now allow you to build customized, app-like experiences within Muse. The new feature, called "spaces," allows its AI assistant to build things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, music tracker, trivia game, and more, which you can interact with directly in the Muse app. Meta says you can create a new space by […]

articles.headline: USCIRF officials allege vigilante attacks on gurdwaras in India
articles.title: Two USCIRF officials claim vigilante attacks on gurdwaras in India
articles.summary: Two commissioners from the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) claimed Sikh gurdwaras in India have faced vigilante violence. David Anderson and Joe Grogan urged the U.S. government to pressure New Delhi to protect religious sites and hold perpetrators accountable. India has previously dismissed the USCIRF as a biased organisation lacking credibility.
articles.description: India describes U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom as a biased organisation that lacks credibility

articles.headline: Paraguay faces political crisis as President Santiago Pena faces impeachment
articles.title: How Paraguay’s Ueno collapse is only its latest banking crisis
articles.summary: Paraguay is experiencing a major political crisis following the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank, leading to impeachment proceedings against President Santiago Pena. Regulators placed the bank into resolution after discovering risky insider loans exceeding legal limits. Prosecutors have charged 27 officials and detained several executives, while Congress passed a law to repay depositors through a state-guaranteed fund.
articles.description: President Santiago Pena is under fire over links to parent company of collapsed bank.

articles.headline: Nigerian court invalidates opposition party leadership and presidential candidate nomination
articles.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
articles.summary: Nigeria's Federal High Court dissolved the leadership of the African Democratic Congress and ruled that the presidential nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is invalid. The decision follows a legal challenge regarding internal party procedures. The opposition party stated it will appeal the verdict ahead of the upcoming national elections scheduled for January 16, where Abubakar is running against President Bola Tinubu.
articles.description: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.

articles.headline: ISRO's NVS-03 satellite successfully reaches geosynchronous orbit
articles.title: NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation announced that the NVS-03 satellite successfully reached geosynchronous orbit on November 4, 2026, following four orbit maneuvers with a cumulative liquid apogee motor engine burn of 6,164 seconds. Launched on October 30 by a geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle, the third-generation navigation satellite carries indigenous and procured atomic clocks, an L1 signal, and maintains normal health.
articles.description: ‘Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds; with this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit at an inclination of 29.980,’ said ISRO

articles.headline: Bangladesh security forces rescue fifty seven people during border gun battle
articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.summary: Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 individuals during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers in the Rongikhali hills near the Myanmar border on November 5, 2026. The Inter-Services Public Relations stated that one soldier, 27-year-old Md. Titash Sheikh, was killed during the clash. The operation followed a tip-off that an armed gang had abducted approximately 120 Rohingya refugees and citizens.
articles.description: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

articles.headline: CBI registers bank fraud case against Future Retail and Kishore Biyani
articles.title: CBI books Future Retail, Kishore Biyani, others in ₹904 crore bank fraud case; searches conducted in Mumbai
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation registered a case against Future Retail Limited, promoters Kishore Biyani and Rakesh Biyani, and others for allegedly defrauding the State Bank of India of 904.32 crore rupees. Operating on a complaint from the bank's Mumbai branch, investigators conducted searches on November 6, 2026, seizing documents related to the alleged diversion of sanctioned loan funds to associate entities.
articles.description: SBI alleged that the company failed to utilise the sanctioned funds in accordance with the terms and conditions of the loan facilities

articles.headline: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison
articles.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in 2nd national security case
articles.summary: Prominent activist Joshua Wong received a ten-year prison sentence on November 5, 2026, for his second conviction under a national security law in Hong Kong. Judge William Tam rejected claims that his role was minor and ordered the terms to be served concurrently. Critics argue the case reflects a broader crackdown on dissent, while Beijing maintains the law is essential for city stability.
articles.description: The 30-year-old is already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term for the city's biggest national security case

articles.headline: Metropolitan Police expect additional accusations against convicted sex offender Russell Brand
articles.title: U.K. police expect more cases against celebrity sex convict Russell Brand
articles.summary: London's Metropolitan Police anticipate more women will file accusations against celebrity Russell Brand following his conviction for rape and sexual assaults against four women. Brand, who was remanded in custody ahead of a November 9, 2026 sentencing, faces additional investigations regarding two other women. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and various media organizations have responded to the case by addressing systemic failings within the industry.
articles.description: Russell Brand was remanded in custody and told by the judge he faced a "significant custodial term" at his sentencing on November 9

articles.headline: United States Department of Justice prosecutor Jason Reding Quinones resigns
articles.title: US prosecutor who led Trump-backed election probe exits Justice Department
articles.summary: United States Attorney Jason Reding Quinones resigned from the Department of Justice on Friday following Democratic victories in the midterm elections, according to Attorney General Todd Blanche. Quinones previously oversaw investigations into Russia's role in the 2016 election and the indictment of Raul Castro. His departure coincides with other high-level resignations at the department amid anticipated congressional investigations into federal oversight.
articles.description: Jason Reding Quinones' resignation comes as administration braces for Democrat-led investigations.

articles.headline: Rising feed costs threaten Telangana poultry farmers and increase egg prices
articles.title: When feed prices crack the egg market
articles.summary: Poultry farmers in Telangana face soaring production costs as open-market prices for maize and soybean surge due to El Niño impacts and alleged hoarding. Telangana produces 3.80 crore daily eggs, but steep feed expenses threaten profit margins and output. Industry representatives have requested subsidized grain from the Food Corporation of India to stabilise feed prices ahead of seasonal demand.
articles.description: Rising maize and soybean prices, the mainstays of poultry feed, are squeezing farmers even as El Niño threatens to disrupt grain supplies; with feed accounting for nearly 80% of production costs, the pressure is building on Telangana’s poultry sector, raising concerns over egg output and prices

articles.headline: Jim Messina says numerous Democrats are preparing for 2028 presidential campaigns
articles.title: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
articles.summary: Following successful midterm elections, more than twenty Democratic campaigns are actively preparing for the 2028 presidential race by hiring staff and organizing financing, according to former Barack Obama aide Jim Messina. Speaking on the BBC podcast Americast, Messina noted that candidates focused successfully on economic issues and Donald Trump tariffs, though party leaders now face the challenge of uniting progressive and centrist factions in Congress.
articles.description: Jim Messina tells the BBC that after Democrats' midterm victories he's talked to "over two dozen campaigns", with some already hiring staff.

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy hopes United States Democratic midterm victory increases support for Ukraine
articles.title: Zelenskyy hopes Democratic Congress will bring more US help for Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Democratic gains in the United States midterm elections could increase military and financial assistance for Kyiv. Speaking on November 4, 2026, after voters handed Congress control to the Democrats, Zelenskyy expressed optimism that stronger American backing would influence Russian President Vladimir Putin to help end the ongoing European conflict.
articles.description: EU officials also urge new US Congress to step up pressure on Russia to end the four-and-a-half-year war.

articles.headline: Karnataka lab tests reveal petrol ethanol blends exceeding twenty percent
articles.title: Lab tests show ethanol blend in E20 petrol as high as 31% in Karnataka
articles.summary: Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad announced on November 6, 2026, that laboratory tests showed ethanol blending in petrol reached up to 31.2 percent across several districts. Arshad criticized oil marketing companies for lacking transparency and demanded Union Government compensation for consumers whose vehicles face potential damage from excessive ethanol concentrations exceeding permitted limits.
articles.description: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka demands penalising OMCs, an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers

articles.headline: Election Commission of India reopens enrolment for excluded Telangana voters
articles.title: ECI reopens the doors for voters excluded from draft electoral roll
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India has provided an additional opportunity for voters excluded from the draft electoral roll under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate category to register for final rolls. Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudharsan Reddy directed district officials to ensure compliance with the process, which must be completed by November 21, 2026, following observations made by the Supreme Court.

articles.headline: Taiwan closes its Papua New Guinea representative office citing Chinese pressure
articles.title: Taiwan to close representative office in Papua New Guinea, blames China
articles.summary: Taiwan announced the closure of its representative office in Port Moresby and the cessation of liquefied natural gas purchases from Papua New Guinea, attributing the decision to persistent Chinese political pressure. The Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated on Friday that Papua New Guinea had demanded staff departures under a strict deadline. The move also includes terminating technical cooperation and medical missions, ending ties with one of few remaining Pacific partners.
articles.description: Amid the fallout, Taiwan says it will stop purchases of liquefied natural gas from Port Moresby.

articles.headline: Supreme Court says India fertility drop makes two-child penalties outdated
articles.title: Falling fertility rate makes two-child penalties outdated in India, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on November 4, 2026, that laws penalising individuals for having more than two children have lost relevance due to falling fertility rates. A Bench led by Justice P.S. Narasimha stated that the 2003 Javed judgment requires reconsideration as demographic shifts point toward an ageing population. The court protected an elected official from disqualification under the Maharashtra law.
articles.description: ‘The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades’, says Bench

articles.headline: Technology giants gain following United States Democratic midterm election sweep
articles.title: U.S. Democrats' midterm sweep fuels $750 billion Big Tech rally
articles.summary: Shares of major United States technology companies surged on November 5, 2026, following the Democratic Party's midterm election sweep. Investors anticipated that potential curbs on data-centre construction could restrict overbuilding and reduce capital expenditures, boosting market values for firms such as Amazon and Apple while smaller cloud infrastructure competitors experienced significant share price declines.
articles.description: Apple, which has avoided ‌Big Tech’s massive AI spending but is feeling the sting of an AI-fueled surge in memory chip prices, jumped nearly 7% ‌to a record high

articles.title: Mamdani: ‘it’s morning again in America’ after blue wave

articles.headline: Aviation industry faces disruption from a spate of bomb threats
articles.title: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry
articles.summary: The global aviation sector is confronting significant operational challenges after experiencing at least thirty-two bomb threats targeting a dozen carriers over four days. Although all incidents were confirmed hoaxes communicated via phone calls and emails, airlines were forced to implement emergency protocols, resulting in diverted flights and military escorts. Experts note the coordinated nature of the threats mirrors hybrid warfare tactics, with perpetrators remaining difficult to trace.
articles.description: After a week of disruption, airlines are facing both safety and financial concerns.

articles.headline: Jindal SAW to build seamless pipe plant in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Jindal SAW to set up 300,000-tonne seamless pipe plant in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Indian manufacturer Jindal SAW Ltd. announced plans to establish a 300,000-tonne-per-annum seamless pipe manufacturing facility in Abu Dhabi by 2027. Operating via its United Arab Emirates subsidiary at ICAD-II Musaffah, the project aims to utilize Precision Quality Finishing rolling technology. Managing Director Sminu Jindal emphasized disciplined execution to strengthen the company position in the regional energy infrastructure market.
articles.description: The project will be the UAE’s first seamless pipe manufacturing facility using PQF technology and the second of its kind in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region.

articles.headline: Irish government says Europe bomb threats likely co-ordinated campaign
articles.title: Europe bomb threats 'likely co-ordinated campaign': Irish government
articles.summary: Ireland official authorities stated that recent hoax bomb claims targeting domestic media organizations were likely part of a broader co-ordinated campaign of disruption affecting European aviation. The incidents prompted security responses at multiple broadcasters in Dublin. Police and military units are currently collaborating with international counterparts to identify the culprits responsible for the widespread disruptions.
articles.description: The hoaxes in Dublin came as more European flights were also hit on November 6 by bomb threats, the latest this week forcing authorities to reroute some planes or escort civilian aircraft with fighter jets

articles.description: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong, who became the global face of Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement has been sentenced.

articles.headline: ADNOC signs ten-year LNG supply agreement with Gujarat Energy
articles.title: ADNOC inks 10-year LNG supply and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company signed a ten-year sales agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas beginning in 2028. This deal marks the fifth such arrangement between the United Arab Emirates firm and an Indian company, bolstering international trade. Deliveries will be handled through the company global marketing and trading platform and its international investment arm.
articles.description: This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

articles.headline: Bike-taxi driver arrested for allegedly assaulting female passenger
articles.title: Bike-taxi driver held on charge of sexually assaulting woman passenger
articles.summary: Medical College police arrested Jagadeesh of Mankavu on November 6, 2026, following allegations that he sexually assaulted a woman passenger during a ride. According to law enforcement, the incident occurred on November 4 during a journey from Kozhikode to Kottuli, where the victim reported that the online bike-taxi driver repeatedly misbehaved and touched her inappropriately.

articles.headline: Ailing elephant calf airlifted from Keralam to Gujarat for treatment
articles.title: Elephant calf with bone disorder airlifted from Keralam to Vantara in Gujarat for specialised treatment
articles.summary: An 18-month-old elephant calf named Maya was airlifted on November 6, 2026, from Keralam to Vantara in Gujarat for specialised medical care. Abandoned in April and later injured in a fall, the animal suffered from a congenital bone disorder causing severe pain. Following expert assessments, Chief Wildlife Warden P. Pugazhendi arranged the transfer funded entirely by Vantara.
articles.description: The health of the elephant calf, which is unable to stand or walk due to a genetic bone disorder, had been deteriorating following an injury sustained in a fall in July.

articles.headline: Belagavi administration introduces profit-sharing formula to end sugarcane strike
articles.title: Farmers’ stir: Profit-sharing formula in sugarcane pricing introduced in Belagavi breaks deadlock
articles.summary: The Belagavi District Administration resolved a standoff with sugarcane farmers on November 6, 2026, by introducing a profit-sharing pricing model. District in-charge Minister Satish Jarkiholi stated that 29 factories agreed to pay a base price of 3,650 rupees per tonne, with additional profits divided 75 percent to farmers and 25 percent to factories, prompting most farmers to suspend their protests.
articles.description: This initiative succeeded in breaking the deadlock between sugarcane farmers and factories, allowing for the commencement of operations in sugar factories

articles.headline: Vice-President JD Vance blames Iran war for Republican midterm election losses
articles.title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
articles.summary: Vice-President JD Vance publicly attributed the Republican Party's midterm defeat to the ongoing war in Iran, marking a rare departure from President Donald Trump’s foreign policy. While Trump defended the conflict, he acknowledged its electoral impact. Analysts view Vance’s statement as a potential early move to establish a distinct platform for a 2028 presidential bid.
articles.description: The vice-president's blunt assessment of Republican election defeat marked one of the sharpest breaks with a sitting president in recent memory.

articles.headline: Syria and Saudi Arabia sign defence and financial cooperation agreements
articles.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal, agree $403m in loans
articles.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman signed a defence cooperation deal and secured $403 million in Saudi loans for Syrian infrastructure, energy, and healthcare. The agreements follow discussions on regional security and maritime navigation. Syria is currently evaluating potential entry into a mutual defence alliance with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan.
articles.description: Defence cooperation deal signed as Syria's President al-Sharaa visits Riyadh for the second time in less than a month.

articles.headline: Fire at Oil India facility in Assam leaves one dead
articles.title: One killed and six injured in fire at an OIL facility in Assam
articles.summary: A fire at an Oil India Limited installation in Dibrugarh district on November 6, 2026, resulted in one death and six injuries. According to the public sector undertaking, the blaze erupted during maintenance at an indirect bath heater in Tengakhat. Fire services deployed 11 tenders to extinguish the flames by afternoon, and an internal inquiry committee was established to investigate the incident.
articles.description: The oil exploration major said that the fire broke out at an indirect bath heater, which had been isolated since November 4 for maintenance

articles.headline: Danish Supreme Court hears case on controversial non-Western housing law
articles.title: Why is Denmark separating ‘Western’ and ‘non-Western’ citizens?
articles.summary: Seven families are challenging a 2018 Danish law in the Supreme Court that mandates the reduction of social housing in areas with high populations of non-Western residents. Critics argue the policy is discriminatory, while the government maintains it promotes integration. The Court of Justice of the European Union previously noted the criteria could potentially violate discrimination laws.
articles.description: Evicted families take Denmark’s controversial ‘ghetto law’ to the Supreme Court.
