articles.title: After milk and curd, prices of ghee, butter and paneer too up in Karnataka
articles.summary: Following previous hikes on milk and curd by the Karnataka Milk Federation, the Bangalore Urban, Rural & Ramanagara District Co-Operative Milk Producers Societies Union Limited raised prices for ghee, butter, and paneer across the state on November 4, 2026. Industry representatives warned that the adjustments create an additional financial strain for the local hospitality sector.
articles.description: The revised prices, released on November 4, will come into effect across the State on November 5

articles.headline: Palghar villagers and opposition leaders continue fierce resistance against Vadhavan port project
articles.title: Vadhavan port project faces continued resistance from Palghar villagers
articles.summary: Villagers, farmers, and fishing communities gathered near Dahanu on Friday to protest the Vadhavan port project, backed by opposition politicians from parties like Congress and Shiv Sena. Protesters warned that the ₹76,220 crore initiative by the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and Maharashtra Maritime Board will destroy marine life, displace Adivasi lands, and threaten traditional livelihoods.
articles.description: Opposition parties have joined villagers in Palghar who say the ₹76,220-crore Vadhavan port will take their sea, their farms and their futures

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate searches Aryan Hometec locations over alleged fraud
articles.title: Bengaluru cops can’t find builder accused of cheating, but ED does; raids three locations linked to Aryan Hometec in ₹90-crore fraud case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted raids at three locations linked to Aryan Hometec Private Limited, its directors Bharath Reddy, and Rashmi Bharath Reddy. Investigators seized records regarding an alleged ninety-crore rupee fraud and money laundering case. The agency accused the developers of cheating landowner B.G. Anjinappa, failing to deliver apartments, and diverting funds collected from homebuyers to family entities.
articles.description: The money laundering investigation was initiated based on multiple FIRs registered by the police following complaints from a landowner, homebuyers and financial institutions

articles.headline: Brazilian airport torn apart by violent storm
articles.title: Brazilian airport torn apart by violent storm
articles.description: Dramatic footage captured the moment a powerful tornado struck Chapecó Airport in Santa Catarina, Brazil

articles.headline: World record 53 red cards shown in Brazil football match
articles.title: World record 53 red cards shown in Brazil football match
articles.description: Referees have red-carded 53 players and staff after a massive brawl in an under-20s football match in Brazil.

articles.headline: AERB chairperson promises no safety compromises in private nuclear sector
articles.title: Private sector participation in nuclear energy: No compromise on safety aspects, says AERB Chairperson
articles.summary: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board Chairperson A.K. Balasubrahmanian addressed concerns regarding private sector entry into India's nuclear energy sector. Speaking at a symposium organised by the Atomic Energy Retirees’ Association, he assured that safety and regulatory standards will not be diluted while providing an enabling environment for private players to meet the rising power demands of the country.
articles.description: The AERB chairperson’s remarks gain significance in the context of SHANTI Act and the Union government’s policy decision to welcome private players

articles.headline: Mississippi and Alaska Senate races remain uncalled following midterms
articles.title: What’s delaying the US Senate election results in Mississippi and Alaska?
articles.summary: The United States midterm elections concluded with Democrats securing congressional control, but Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain undecided as ballots are processed. Mississippi features a razor-thin margin between candidates Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom, while Alaska utilizes a ranked-choice voting system and faces legal disputes. State officials expect certified results to be finalised by mid-November.
